diseases.name: Substance abuse disorders

diseases.name: Substance-use disorders
diseases.description: Substance-use disorders are conditions characterized by the harmful use of psychoactive substances such as methamphetamine or cocaine.

diseases.name: systemic autoimmune disease
diseases.description: Systemic autoimmune diseases are conditions where the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own tissues.

diseases.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
diseases.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus is a chronic autoimmune disease that can affect various parts of the body.

diseases.name: T-cell leukemia
diseases.description: T-cell leukemia is a cancer of the T lymphocytes.

diseases.name: tauopathies
diseases.description: Tauopathies are a group of neurodegenerative diseases characterized by the aggregation of tau protein.

diseases.name: Tauopathy
diseases.description: Tauopathy is a group of neurodegenerative disorders pathologically characterized by deposits of tau protein in the brain.

diseases.name: Temple syndrome
diseases.description: Temple syndrome is a genomic imprinting disease caused by maternal duplication of human chromosome 14.

diseases.name: teratoma
diseases.description: Teratoma is a type of tumor that can contain several different types of tissue.

diseases.name: testicular germ cell tumors
diseases.description: Testicular germ cell tumors are cancers that develop in the testicles.

diseases.name: testicular germ cell tumours
diseases.description: Testicular germ cell tumours (TGCTs) are cancers that develop from germ cells in the testis.

diseases.name: thyroid cancer
diseases.description: Thyroid cancer is a cancer that starts in the thyroid gland.

diseases.name: tonsillar carcinoma
diseases.description: Tonsillar carcinoma is a type of cancer that originates in the tonsils.

diseases.name: transitional cell carcinoma
diseases.description: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) is a type of cancer that arises from the transitional epithelium, commonly found in the bladder.

diseases.name: Transmissible spongiform encephalopathies
diseases.description: A group of progressive neurodegenerative disorders, including scrapie, attributed to prions.

diseases.name: Triple-negative breast cancer
diseases.description: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype of breast cancer characterized by the lack of estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2 expression.

diseases.name: Trisomy
diseases.description: Trisomy is a type of aneuploidy where there are three copies of a particular chromosome instead of the normal two.

diseases.name: tuberous sclerosis
diseases.description: Tuberous sclerosis is a neurodevelopmental disorder.

diseases.name: tumor
diseases.description: Tumor refers to an abnormal mass of tissue resulting from uncontrolled cell growth.

diseases.name: tumor diseases
diseases.description: Tumor diseases refer to various types of cancers or neoplasms.

diseases.name: tumor progression
diseases.description: Tumor progression refers to the process by which a tumor grows, invades surrounding tissues, and potentially metastasizes.

diseases.name: tumorigenesis
diseases.description: Tumorigenesis is the process by which normal cells are transformed into cancer cells.

diseases.name: tumors
diseases.description: Tumors are abnormal growths of tissue that can be benign or malignant.

diseases.name: Turner syndrome
diseases.description: Turner syndrome is a chromosomal disorder characterized by the partial or complete absence of one X chromosome in females.

diseases.name: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
diseases.description: Type 1 diabetes mellitus is an autoimmune disorder characterized by the destruction of insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas.

diseases.name: type 2 diabetes (T2D)
diseases.description: Type 2 diabetes is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency.

diseases.name: type 2 diabetes mellitus
diseases.description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency.

diseases.name: ulcerative colitis
diseases.description: Ulcerative colitis is an inflammatory bowel disease that causes inflammation and ulcers in the digestive tract.

diseases.name: upper gastrointestinal cancer
diseases.description: Upper gastrointestinal cancer includes esophageal and gastric cancers.

diseases.name: Urothelial carcinoma
diseases.description: Urothelial carcinoma is a type of cancer that originates in the urothelial cells lining the urinary tract, including the bladder.

diseases.name: Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC)
diseases.description: Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma.

diseases.name: uveal melanoma
diseases.description: Uveal melanoma is a type of cancer that forms in the eye's uvea.

diseases.name: various severe diseases
diseases.description: Various severe diseases can be caused by LINE-1 retrotransposition.

diseases.name: Waardenburg syndrome
diseases.description: Waardenburg syndrome is a genetic disorder characterized by sensorineural hearing loss and pigmentary abnormalities, often associated with neural crest cell defects.

diseases.name: well-differentiated liposarcoma
diseases.description: Well-differentiated liposarcoma is the most common subtype of liposarcoma, a soft tissue sarcoma.

diseases.name: Williams syndrome
diseases.description: Williams syndrome is a developmental disorder that affects many parts of the body, characterized by mild to moderate intellectual disability or learning problems.

diseases.name: Williams-Beuren syndrome
diseases.description: Williams-Beuren syndrome is a developmental disorder caused by a microdeletion on chromosome 7q11.23.

diseases.name: X-linked agammaglobulinemia
diseases.description: X-linked agammaglobulinemia is an immunodeficiency disorder caused by mutations in the BTK gene.

diseases.name: X-linked dilated cardiomyopathy
diseases.description: X-linked dilated cardiomyopathy (XLDCM) is a clinical phenotype of dystrophinopathy characterized by preferential myocardial involvement without overt clinical signs of skeletal myopathy.

diseases.name: X-linked dystonia parkinsonism (XDP)
diseases.description: X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism (XDP, DYT3) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the clinical onset with dystonia followed by parkinsonism, endemic in the Philippine island of Panay.

diseases.name: X-linked Kallmann syndrome
diseases.description: X-linked Kallmann syndrome is a genetic disorder characterized by hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia.

diseases.name: X-linked retinitis pigmentosa 2
diseases.description: X-linked retinitis pigmentosa 2 is a form of progressive retinal degeneration caused by mutations in the RP2 gene.

diseases.name: xeroderma pigmentosum
diseases.description: Xeroderma pigmentosum is a DNA repair-deficiency disorder characterized by extreme sensitivity to ultraviolet light and a high risk of skin cancer.

diseases.name: yolk sac tumor
diseases.description: Yolk sac tumor is a type of malignant germ cell tumor.

diseases.name: α-1 antitrypsin deficiency
diseases.description: α-1 antitrypsin deficiency is a genetic disorder caused by mutations in the SERPINA1 gene.

diseases.name: β-thalassemia
diseases.description: β-thalassemia is one of the most common genetic diseases worldwide, caused by mutations in the human hemoglobin beta (HBB) gene.
diseases.disease_class: Diseases of the blood or blood-forming organs

functions.name: 3' end processing
functions.description: 3' end processing refers to the molecular mechanism that determines the termination point of LINE-1 retrotransposition, which can involve bypassing the primary polyadenylation signal.

functions.name: 3' flanking sequence mobilization
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposition-competent L1s can mobilize and retrotranspose non-L1 sequences located downstream (3') of their own genomic location to new genomic sites.

functions.name: 3' poly(A) tract requirement
functions.description: The presence of a 3' polyadenosine tract is critical for the retrotransposition of LINE-1 and its trans-mobilized targets.

functions.name: 3' transduction
functions.description: A process mediated by the L1 machinery where neighboring, nonrepetitive sequences are mobilized along with the L1 element.

functions.name: 3' UTR stem-loop structure
functions.description: A conserved RNA secondary structure at the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of L1 and Alu elements, hypothesized to be recognized by the LINE-1 reverse transcriptase.

functions.name: 3' UTR-mediated posttranscriptional gene regulation
functions.description: Posttranscriptional control of mRNA subcellular localization, stability, and translation mediated via recognition of a given mRNA transcript's 3' untranslated region (UTR) by microRNAs and RNA-binding proteins.

functions.name: 3'-end stem-loop formation
functions.description: 3'-end stem-loop formation refers to the folding of the 3' end of an RNA or DNA molecule into a secondary structure consisting of a base-paired stem and a single-stranded loop.

functions.name: 3D chromatin architecture
functions.description: 3D chromatin architecture refers to the three-dimensional organization of chromatin within the nucleus.

functions.name: 3D chromatin structure formation
functions.description: 3D chromatin structure formation refers to the spatial organization of chromatin within the nucleus, which influences gene regulation.

functions.name: 3D genome architecture influence
functions.description: The process by which transposons affect the three-dimensional spatial organization of the genome within the nucleus.

functions.name: 3D genome reorganization
functions.description: 3D genome reorganization refers to changes in the three-dimensional architecture of chromatin, including enhancer-promoter loops and topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries.

functions.name: 3D nuclear organization
functions.description: 3D nuclear organization refers to the spatial arrangement of chromatin and nuclear compartments within the nucleus.

functions.name: 5' and 3' transduction
functions.description: 5' and 3' transductions refer to the non-L1 genomic sequences flanking an L1 insertion, which are co-mobilized during retrotransposition.

functions.name: 5' end microhomology
functions.description: 5' end microhomology refers to short stretches of sequence identity between the 5' end of a new L1 integrant and the target DNA sequence.

functions.name: 5' flanking sequence transduction
functions.description: 5' flanking sequence transduction is a process where SVA elements acquire and transduce 5' promoter sequences from external cellular promoters.

functions.name: 5' integration
functions.description: 5' integration refers to the molecular mechanism by which the 5' end of a LINE element is integrated into the host chromosome during retrotransposition.

functions.name: 5' inversion
functions.description: A genomic rearrangement where the 5' segment of a retrotransposed element is inverted relative to the 3' segment, resulting in a head-to-head orientation.

functions.name: 5' junction formation
functions.description: 5' junction formation refers to the mechanism for joining the retrotransposon to the target site at the 5' end during retrotransposition.

functions.name: 5' transduction
functions.description: 5'-transduction is a mechanism where a retrotransposon captures and mobilizes upstream genomic sequences during its insertion.

functions.name: 5' truncation
functions.description: 5' truncation is a common outcome of LINE-1 retrotransposition, often generating elements with truncated 5' ends flanked by target site duplications (TSDs).

functions.name: 5'-end attachment
functions.description: The process of linking the 5'-end of a nascent retrotransposon copy to its genomic target site.

functions.name: 5'-end joining
functions.description: The molecular mechanism responsible for generating the 5' junctions of LINE inserts.

functions.name: 5'-end-joining pathway
functions.description: The 5'-end-joining pathway is a molecular mechanism involved in the integration of LINE elements into host chromosomal DNA.

functions.name: 5'-inverted insertion
functions.description: A type of retrotransposed insertion structure characterized by an inverted 5' end.

functions.name: 5'-truncated insertion
functions.description: 5'-truncated insertion is a type of de novo LINE-1 insertion where the 5' end of the element is missing.

functions.name: 5-methylcytosine-associated mutations (MAM)
functions.description: Mutations, specifically C to T transitions, that are potentially associated with the deamination of 5-methylcytosine.

functions.name: A-tail expansion
functions.description: The lengthening of the poly(A) tail of a retrotransposon, which in Alu elements occurs during insertion due to slippage by the L1 ORF2 protein.

functions.name: A-to-I RNA editing
functions.description: Adenosine-to-inosine editing of RNA, which can affect RNA structure and stability.

functions.name: aberrant activation
functions.description: Aberrant activation refers to the abnormal or dysregulated expression or activity of a gene or element, such as HERVs.

functions.name: aberrant activity
functions.description: Aberrant activity refers to abnormal or dysregulated biological function, such as uncontrolled transposition.

functions.name: aberrant DNA methylation
functions.description: Aberrant DNA methylation refers to abnormal patterns of DNA methylation, such as the hypomethylation of retrotransposons, which occurs during malignant cell transformation.

functions.name: Aberrant epigenetic changes
functions.description: Aberrant epigenetic changes refer to abnormal patterns of DNA methylation, histone modification, or chromatin structure that disrupt normal gene regulation.

functions.name: aberrant expression
functions.description: Aberrant expression refers to abnormal levels of gene or transposon expression, which can be either overexpression or underexpression compared to normal conditions.

functions.name: Aberrant gene expression
functions.description: Aberrant gene expression refers to abnormal levels or patterns of gene transcription.

functions.name: aberrant gene regulation
functions.description: Aberrant gene regulation refers to the disruption of normal gene expression patterns.

functions.name: aberrant immune responses
functions.description: Aberrant immune responses are inappropriate or chronic immune system reactions.

functions.name: Aberrant mRNA splicing
functions.description: Aberrant mRNA splicing refers to the production of abnormal mRNA transcripts due to disruptions in the normal splicing process.

functions.name: aberrant oncogene activation
functions.description: Aberrant oncogene activation is the inappropriate or dysregulated transcriptional activation of genes that can promote cancer development.

functions.name: Aberrant proliferation
functions.description: Aberrant proliferation refers to abnormal and uncontrolled cell division.

functions.name: aberrant reactivation
functions.description: Aberrant reactivation refers to the inappropriate re-expression of normally silenced genetic elements.

functions.name: Aberrant recombination
functions.description: Aberrant recombination refers to abnormal genetic recombination events, which can be facilitated by elements like LINE-1.

functions.name: aberrant regulation
functions.description: Aberrant regulation of transposable elements can result in deleterious effects.

functions.name: Aberrant RNA splicing
functions.description: Aberrant RNA splicing is a process where errors in pre-mRNA splicing lead to the production of abnormal mRNA isoforms.

functions.name: aberrant splice-site activation
functions.description: Aberrant splice-site activation is the process where a cryptic or non-canonical splice site is used, often due to mutations, leading to altered mRNA splicing.

functions.name: Aberrant splicing
functions.description: Aberrant splicing refers to the formation of non-canonical RNA transcripts due to the use of alternative splice or polyadenylation signals.

functions.name: aberrant THE1B fusion transcript expression
functions.description: Aberrant THE1B fusion transcript expression refers to the elevated or dysregulated expression of THE1B-containing fusion transcripts in disease states.

functions.name: Aberrant transcription
functions.description: Aberrant transcription refers to abnormal gene expression patterns, such as decreased expression of specific isoforms.

functions.name: Aberrant transcription start site (TSS) usage
functions.description: Initiation of transcription from non-canonical or alternative start sites.

functions.name: Aberrant upregulation
functions.description: Aberrant upregulation refers to an abnormal increase in the expression level of a gene or genomic element.

functions.name: abnormal DNA rearrangement
functions.description: Abnormal DNA rearrangement refers to genomic alterations such as deletions, insertions, or translocations that deviate from the normal structure.

functions.name: abnormal gene expression
functions.description: Abnormal gene expression refers to the dysregulation of gene transcription levels.

functions.name: Abnormal overexpression
functions.description: Abnormal overexpression refers to the significantly increased expression level of a gene or element compared to normal conditions.

functions.name: abnormal programming
functions.description: Abnormal programming refers to the incorrect establishment or alteration of epigenetic or other regulatory patterns during development.

functions.name: Abnormal splicing
functions.description: Abnormal splicing is a disruption of the normal RNA splicing process, often leading to aberrant transcripts.

functions.name: abscopal effect
functions.description: The abscopal effect is a phenomenon where localized radiotherapy induces systemic anti-tumor effects at distant, non-irradiated sites.

functions.name: Accumulation
functions.description: Accumulation refers to the process of gathering or increasing in number over time.

functions.name: Accumulation of heritable L1 insertions
functions.description: The accumulation of heritable L1 insertions refers to the build-up of LINE-1 insertions that are passed on to offspring.

functions.name: Accumulation of somatic insertions
functions.description: Accumulation of somatic insertions refers to the time-dependent increase in the number of new transposon insertions within the genomes of somatic cells.

functions.name: accumulation on the X chromosome
functions.description: The process by which transposable elements, such as LINE-1, become enriched on the X chromosome.

functions.name: Acquired chromosomal aberrations
functions.description: Acquired chromosomal aberrations are structural or numerical changes in chromosomes that occur somatically, not inherited through the germline.

functions.name: Acquisition of erythroid dominant expression
functions.description: Acquisition of erythroid dominant expression refers to the evolutionary gain of tissue-specific (erythroid) gene expression patterns, potentially mediated by regulatory element insertion.

functions.name: activating oncogenic transcriptional factors
functions.description: Activating oncogenic transcriptional factors is a process that increases the activity of transcription factors that promote cancer development.

functions.name: Activating p120-ctn/Rac1/Cdc42 axis
functions.description: Triggering the activation of the Rho GTPase signaling pathway downstream of p120-catenin, involving Rac1 and Cdc42.

functions.name: Activation
functions.description: The process of becoming active or expressed, as observed for transposable elements in the blood of C9orf72 expansion carriers.

functions.name: activation mutagenesis screen
functions.description: Activation mutagenesis screen is a forward genetic approach using transposons to randomly activate gene expression and identify genes conferring specific phenotypes, such as drug resistance.

functions.name: activation of cGAS-STING pathway
functions.description: The process of triggering the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) innate immune signaling pathway.

functions.name: activation of dormant repeat elements
functions.description: Activation of dormant repeat elements refers to the undesirable reactivation of transposable elements due to loss of epigenetic silencing.

functions.name: Activation of gene expression
functions.description: The process of increasing the transcription of cellular genes.

functions.name: activation of L1s
functions.description: Activation of L1s refers to the process by which LINE-1 retrotransposons become transcriptionally and transpositionally active, often due to epigenetic changes like hypomethylation.

functions.name: activation of MDA5
functions.description: The process by which the innate immune receptor MDA5 is activated, typically by binding to double-stranded RNA.

functions.name: Activation of mobile elements
functions.description: Activation of mobile elements refers to the process by which transposons become transcriptionally and/or transpositionally active in somatic cells.

functions.name: Activation of p120-ctn/Rac1/Cdc42 axis
functions.description: LncMER52A triggers the activation of Rho GTPase downstream of p120-catenin, specifically the p120-ctn/Rac1/Cdc42 axis.

functions.name: activation of pluripotency genes
functions.description: Activation of pluripotency genes refers to the process of turning on genes that are essential for maintaining the pluripotent state of stem cells.

functions.name: Activation of proinflammatory transposable elements
functions.description: The process by which transposable elements are activated and contribute to an inflammatory state.

functions.name: Activation of the cGAS-STING cascade
functions.description: Activation of the cGAS-STING cascade is an innate immune response pathway triggered by cytoplasmic nucleic acids, such as those from transposable elements.

functions.name: Activation of the host genome
functions.description: The process of initiating transcriptional activity in the host genome during developmental stages like totipotency.

functions.name: activation of the innate immune system
functions.description: Activation of the innate immune system is a cellular response that can be triggered by transposable element activity.

functions.name: activation of tumor-suppressive mechanisms
functions.description: The initiation of cellular processes, such as p53 and interferon responses, that inhibit tumor development.

functions.name: Activation of young LINE-1
functions.description: The process by which young LINE-1 elements become transcriptionally active and potentially mobile.

functions.name: Active L1 unit
functions.description: The 'active L1 unit' refers to the actively transposable form of the LINE-1 element, which may retain features enabling recent transposition.

functions.name: Active LINE-1 expression
functions.description: Active LINE-1 expression refers to transcription initiated from the internal promoter of a LINE-1 element.

functions.name: active retrotransposition
functions.description: Active retrotransposition refers to the ongoing process of LINE-1 elements copying and inserting themselves into new genomic locations.

functions.name: Active reverse transcriptase activity
functions.description: Active reverse transcriptase activity refers to the enzymatic function that synthesizes DNA from an RNA template, essential for retrotransposition.

functions.name: Adaptive evolution
functions.description: Adaptive evolution is the process by which organisms become better suited to their environment through genetic changes.

functions.name: ADAR1 editing
functions.description: ADAR1 editing refers to the adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing activity performed by ADAR1, which can alter RNA structure and sequence.

functions.name: adenosinergic immunometabolic suppression
functions.description: Adenosinergic immunometabolic suppression refers to the immunosuppressive effects mediated by adenosine in the tumor microenvironment.

functions.name: adjacent genes expression
functions.description: Adjacent genes expression refers to the transcriptional activity of genes located near LINE-1 insertion sites.

functions.name: Adoptive immunotherapy
functions.description: Adoptive immunotherapy is a treatment that uses a patient's own immune cells, such as T cells, to fight disease.

functions.name: adoptive NK cell immunotherapy
functions.description: Adoptive NK cell immunotherapy involves the transfer of engineered or activated natural killer cells to a patient to treat diseases such as cancer.

functions.name: Affect gene expression
functions.description: LINE elements can modulate the transcription levels of human genes.

functions.name: affect gene transcription
functions.description: Affect gene transcription refers to the process by which transposable elements can influence the expression of genes.

functions.name: Affect neighboring gene expression
functions.description: The process by which the activity of a genetic element influences the expression levels of genes located in its genomic vicinity.

functions.name: Affect protein sequences
functions.description: LINE elements can alter the amino acid sequence of proteins.

functions.name: affect somatic genome structure and function
functions.description: The process by which LINE-1 activity influences the architecture and operation of somatic cell genomes.

functions.name: Affect splicing patterns
functions.description: LINE elements can influence the alternative splicing of gene transcripts.

functions.name: affecting gene expression or regulation
functions.description: This refers to the process by which the insertion of a transposon can alter the normal expression patterns or regulatory mechanisms of nearby genes.

functions.name: Affecting gene regulation
functions.description: Influencing the control of when, where, and how much a gene is expressed.

functions.name: Age estimation of retrotransposon subfamilies
functions.description: Age estimation of retrotransposon subfamilies is a method to determine the time since a retrotransposon subfamily began proliferating in a genome.

functions.name: Aging
functions.description: Aging is the progressive decline in physiological function associated with the passage of time.

functions.name: aging-associated myeloid-biased hematopoiesis
functions.description: A shift in blood cell production towards the myeloid lineage that occurs with aging.

functions.name: AGO2-mediated repression
functions.description: Gene repression mediated by Argonaute 2 (AGO2) targeting intronic L1 pre-mRNA complexes.

functions.name: AhR signaling
functions.description: AhR signaling is a pathway activated by ligands binding to the aryl hydrocarbon receptor, influencing gene expression.

functions.name: AKT signaling activation
functions.description: AKT signaling activation is a beneficial pathway for cardiac regeneration.

functions.name: alter gene expression
functions.description: Alteration of gene expression refers to changes in the level at which a gene is transcribed.

functions.name: alteration of epigenetic regulations
functions.description: Alteration of epigenetic regulations involves changes in heritable gene expression patterns not caused by changes in DNA sequence.

functions.name: Alteration of expression profile
functions.description: Alteration of expression profile refers to changes in the pattern, level, or timing of gene expression.

functions.name: alteration of gene expression
functions.description: Alteration of gene expression refers to changes in the level or pattern of gene transcription, which can be caused by transposon insertion into regulatory regions.

functions.name: alteration of genomic landscape
functions.description: Changes to the structure and organization of the genome, contributed by the mobilization of transposable elements.

functions.name: Alteration of splicing
functions.description: Alteration of splicing refers to changes in the process that removes introns and joins exons from pre-mRNA to form mature mRNA.

functions.name: Alteration of target gene expression
functions.description: Changes in the expression levels of genes, potentially caused by the insertion or activity of nearby elements like transposons.

functions.name: Alteration of transcription initiation
functions.description: Alteration of transcription initiation refers to changes in the process that determines where and when gene transcription begins.

functions.name: alterations in target gene expression
functions.description: Alterations in target gene expression refer to changes in the level or pattern of gene expression, potentially caused by retrotransposon insertion.

functions.name: alterations to normal splicing patterns
functions.description: A mechanism where SVA insertions disrupt the normal process of RNA splicing.

functions.name: altered DNA methylation
functions.description: Altered DNA methylation is a change in the methylation pattern of DNA.

functions.name: altered expression
functions.description: Altered expression refers to changes in the normal level of transcription or activity of transposable elements.

functions.name: Altered gene expression
functions.description: Altered gene expression refers to changes in the transcription or splicing of a gene, potentially leading to abnormal transcript isoforms.

functions.name: Altered gene transcription
functions.description: Altered gene transcription refers to changes in the rate or pattern of gene expression.

functions.name: altered genetic networks
functions.description: Altered genetic networks refer to changes in the complex interactions between genes and their products.

functions.name: Altered retrotransposon expression
functions.description: Changes in the expression levels of retrotransposons, which may be associated with disease states.

functions.name: Altered splicing
functions.description: Altered splicing refers to changes in the RNA splicing patterns, which can be caused by transposon insertions.

functions.name: altering gene expression
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposons modify the level or pattern of gene transcription.

functions.name: alternate transcript activation
functions.description: Alternate transcript activation refers to the initiation of transcription from an alternative promoter or start site, leading to a different RNA transcript.

functions.name: Alternative endonuclease activity (alt-EN)
functions.description: An endonuclease activity associated with the L1 ORF2p protein that is distinct from the canonical endonuclease domain activity and is evolutionarily conserved within the reverse transcriptase fold.

functions.name: alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT)
functions.description: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) is a telomere maintenance mechanism used by some cancer cells that do not express telomerase.

functions.name: alternative mRNA transcript formation
functions.description: Alternative mRNA transcript formation is the generation of different mRNA variants from a single gene.

functions.name: Alternative promoter
functions.description: Alternative promoter refers to the use of different transcription start sites for a gene.

functions.name: alternative promoter activation
functions.description: Alternative promoter activation refers to the initiation of transcription from a non-canonical promoter site, such as those within transposable elements.

functions.name: Alternative promoter function
functions.description: L1 ASP can function as an alternative promoter for host genes, generating chimeric transcripts with coding regions identical to the host gene's ORF.

functions.name: alternative promoter usage
functions.description: Alternative promoter usage is a mechanism where different promoters drive the expression of distinct isoforms of the same gene.

functions.name: alternative promoters identification
functions.description: The process of identifying different transcription start sites for a single gene, leading to variant transcripts.

functions.name: alternative protein isoform production
functions.description: The production of alternative protein isoforms from a single gene, often driven by different promoters, leading to proteins with distinct functions.

functions.name: Alternative RNA splicing at cryptic splice sites
functions.description: Alternative RNA splicing at cryptic splice sites is a mechanism involved in SVA-mediated 5' transduction events.

functions.name: Alternative sense promoter activity
functions.description: A potential promoter activity within the internal part of the LINE-1 5'-UTR that may drive the synthesis of a 5'-truncated mRNA.

functions.name: Alternative splicing
functions.description: Alternative splicing is a process that generates different mRNA isoforms from a single gene, with specific events altered in SETMAR knockout cell lines.

functions.name: Alternative splicing and polyadenylation
functions.description: Alternative splicing and polyadenylation is a mechanism that generates multiple RNA transcripts from a single gene locus.

functions.name: Alternative transcriptional termination
functions.description: Alternative transcriptional termination refers to the use of different transcription termination sites for a gene.

functions.name: Alu insertion
functions.description: Alu insertion is the process by which Alu retrotransposons integrate into new genomic locations, often mediated by the LINE-1 machinery.

functions.name: Alu insertion polymorphism
functions.description: Alu insertion polymorphism refers to the presence or absence of an Alu element at a specific genomic locus, representing a form of genetic variation in human populations.

functions.name: Alu mobilization
functions.description: Alu mobilization is the process of Alu retrotransposition, which is driven by the LINE-1 ORF2 protein.

functions.name: Alu recombination-mediated deletion (ARMD)
functions.description: Alu recombination-mediated deletion is a genomic deletion event caused by recombination between Alu elements.

functions.name: Alu replication cycle shunt
functions.description: A proposed alternative pathway for Alu element propagation involving cytoplasmic cDNA synthesis, distinct from canonical retrotransposition.

functions.name: Alu retrotransposition
functions.description: Alu retrotransposition is the process by which Alu elements mobilize within the genome via an RNA intermediate.

functions.name: Alu trans-mobilization
functions.description: Alu trans-mobilization is the process by which the LINE-1 ORF2 protein machinery mobilizes non-autonomous Alu elements.

functions.name: Alu transcription
functions.description: Alu transcription is the process of generating RNA from the Alu promoter.

functions.name: Alu-Alu recombination
functions.description: Alu-Alu recombination is a form of unequal homologous recombination between Alu elements that can lead to genomic rearrangements.

functions.name: Alu-induced mutagenesis
functions.description: The process of mutation generation caused by the insertion or activity of Alu retrotransposons.

functions.name: Alu-mediated deletion
functions.description: Alu-mediated deletion is a genomic deletion event caused by recombination between Alu elements.

functions.name: Alu-mediated recombination
functions.description: Alu-mediated recombination is a genomic rearrangement process facilitated by homologous sequences between Alu elements.

functions.name: Alu/Alu homologous recombination
functions.description: A recombination event between homologous Alu elements, which can lead to genomic rearrangements.

functions.name: Amber suppression
functions.description: Amber suppression is a technique that allows the incorporation of noncanonical amino acids into proteins by reassigning the amber stop codon (UAG) to code for an amino acid.

functions.name: amino acid substitution
functions.description: Amino acid substitution refers to changes in the protein sequence of a gene, which can indicate evolutionary selection pressure.

functions.name: AMPK activation
functions.description: AMPK activation is the process of activating AMP-activated protein kinase, a master metabolic regulator, often in response to cellular stress.

functions.name: AMPK signaling
functions.description: AMPK signaling is a cellular energy-sensing pathway activated by exercise and metabolic stress.

functions.name: Amplification
functions.description: Amplification refers to the process of increasing the copy number of a gene or DNA sequence.

functions.name: Amplification burst
functions.description: Amplification burst refers to a period of high activity and copy number increase for a transposable element family.

functions.name: ancestral insertion
functions.description: Ancestral insertion refers to a transposon insertion event that occurred in a common ancestor of a population and is now fixed or polymorphic in that population.

functions.name: Ancestral recombination
functions.description: Ancestral recombination refers to historical recombination events that have shaped the mosaic structure of haplotypes.

functions.name: anchorage-independent growth

functions.description: A cis-regulatory role refers to the function of a DNA sequence in regulating the expression of nearby genes.

functions.name: Cleavage
functions.description: Cleavage refers to the enzymatic cutting of DNA strands, such as at the ends of a transposon during transposition.

functions.name: Cleavage-stage transcriptional program
functions.description: Cleavage-stage transcriptional program refers to the specific set of genes and elements activated during the early cleavage stages of embryonic development.

functions.name: clonal amplification
functions.description: Clonal amplification refers to the expansion of a cell lineage containing a specific genetic alteration, such as a retrotransposon insertion.

functions.name: Clonal expansion
functions.description: Clonal expansion is the process by which a cell with a specific mutation gives rise to a population of identical daughter cells.

functions.name: clonal fixation
functions.description: Clonal fixation refers to a somatic mutation becoming present in all cells of a tumor clone.

functions.name: Cluster-independent piRNA production
functions.description: A mode of piRNA production that targets young TEs without involving piRNA clusters, present at both prenatal and postnatal stages of spermatogenesis.

functions.name: Clustered transposon insertion
functions.description: Clustered transposon insertion is the phenomenon where multiple transposon insertions occur in close genomic proximity.

functions.name: CNCC specification
functions.description: Cranial neural crest cell (CNCC) specification is the process critical for vertebrate craniofacial development where cells acquire their specific identity and fate.

functions.name: Co-evolution
functions.description: Coevolution refers to the reciprocal evolutionary change between interacting species or genetic elements, such as between LINE-1 and Alu.

functions.name: co-expression of transposable elements
functions.description: Co-expression of transposable elements refers to the simultaneous transcription of different transposon families or sub-families within the same cell.

functions.name: co-expression of TRPV1 and TRPV3
functions.description: The coordinated expression of the TRPV1 and TRPV3 genes in multiple human tissues.

functions.name: co-expression with downstream genes
functions.description: Co-expression with downstream genes refers to the coordinated transcription of a transposable element and neighboring genes.

functions.name: Co-integration
functions.description: Co-integration is the process where two or more distinct DNA sequences are integrated together into a new genomic location.

functions.name: Co-option
functions.description: Co-option is the evolutionary process by which a transposable element is recruited for a new function, such as gene regulation.

functions.name: co-option/exaptation
functions.description: The evolutionary process where a genetic sequence, originally with one function (or no function), is recruited for a new, beneficial function in the host organism.

functions.name: Co-repression of genes
functions.description: Co-repression of genes refers to the joint silencing of genes by multiple factors.

functions.name: Coating the RNA
functions.description: Coating the RNA is a proposed role for the ORF1 protein (ORF1p) during L1 retrotransposition.

functions.name: Coclustering
functions.description: Coclustering refers to the tendency of most Alu elements to be located near each other in the genome.

functions.name: coding sequence disruption
functions.description: Coding sequence disruption occurs when a retrotransposon inserts into a gene and interrupts its coding sequence.

functions.name: Cognitive function
functions.description: Cognitive function refers to mental processes in the brain, including attention, impulsivity, and working memory.

functions.name: Coiled-coil domain stability and dynamics
functions.description: The structural integrity and conformational flexibility of the three-stranded coiled-coil (3SCC) domain in ORF1p.

functions.name: Colocalization with immune response genes
functions.description: The genomic positioning of HERV and MaLR loci near genes that are involved and modulated in the immune response.

functions.name: Colonization of the human genome by mobile genetic elements
functions.description: The process by which mobile genetic elements, such as retrotransposons, accumulate and occupy a significant portion of the human genome.

functions.name: Compartmentalization of translation
functions.description: The spatial organization of protein synthesis, such as translation on free cytoplasmic ribosomes versus membrane-bound ribosomes.

functions.name: competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) activity
functions.description: Competitive endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs) compete for the binding of the same set of miRNAs targeting protein coding genes, thereby regulating their expression.

functions.name: Competitive recruitment of transcription factors
functions.description: A process where a DNA element binds and sequesters transcription factors, affecting their availability at other genomic sites.

functions.name: Competitive relationships between TEs
functions.description: Interactions where different transposable elements may compete for host resources or regulatory systems.

functions.name: Complementation in trans
functions.description: Complementation in trans is a copying mechanism where elements are copied by other elements of the same family.

functions.name: Complex assembly
functions.description: Complex assembly is a divalent metal ion-dependent step involving transposase and the transposon end(s) prior to the first catalytic step.

functions.name: complex rearrangement
functions.description: Complex rearrangement refers to a genomic alteration involving multiple breakpoints and/or non-homologous end joining, often leading to deletions or duplications.

functions.name: complex translocation
functions.description: Complex translocation involves the exchange of genetic material between two or more chromosomes in a non-reciprocal or intricate manner.

functions.name: computational analysis of NGS data
functions.description: Bioinformatic methods used to process and interpret data from next-generation sequencing experiments.

functions.name: Concerted evolution
functions.description: Concerted evolution is a process that maintains sequence homogeneity among members of a multigene family, such as the RNU2 locus.

functions.name: Conditional knockout
functions.description: Conditional knockout is a method to inactivate a gene in a specific tissue or at a specific time.

functions.name: Conformational change
functions.description: A significant conformational change between first- and second-strand cleavage at each transposon end is proposed for mariner excision.

functions.name: Conservation
functions.description: The evolutionary process by which a genetic feature is maintained in a population due to selective pressure.

functions.name: Conserved expression
functions.description: Conserved expression refers to the pattern of gene or transcript expression that is maintained across different species.

functions.name: conserved structural features of non-LTR-retroelement RTs
Constitutive splicing
functions.description: Constitutive splicing refers to exons that are always included in the mature mRNA transcript.

functions.name: Contact domain boundary formation
functions.description: The creation of boundaries between topologically associating domains (TADs) in the genome.

functions.name: containment of regulatory elements
functions.description: The property of SVA retrotransposons, such as SVA D, to harbor DNA sequences that can regulate reporter gene expression in vitro.

functions.name: Contribute coding sequences
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposons provide protein-coding sequences to the genome.

functions.name: Contribute regulatory sequences
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposons provide regulatory elements (e.g., promoters, enhancers) to the genome.

functions.name: Contribute to phenotypic heterogeneity
functions.description: SINEs can serve as beneficial building blocks that contribute to diversity in observable traits.

functions.name: contributing to aging
functions.description: L1's contributions to aging processes is an area of active research.

functions.name: contributing to aging diseases
functions.description: L1's contributions to aging diseases is an area of active research.

functions.name: contributing to genetic innovation
functions.description: The role of retrotransposons in introducing new genetic material or regulatory sequences that can drive evolutionary change.

functions.name: Contributing to regulatory elements near quantitative trait loci (QTLs)
functions.description: The function of being part of genomic elements that regulate gene expression and are located near loci associated with quantitative traits.

functions.name: control expression of protein-coding genes
functions.description: Control of expression of protein-coding genes refers to the regulation of transcription levels of genes that encode proteins.

functions.name: control of stemness
functions.description: Control of stemness refers to the regulation of properties associated with stem cells, such as self-renewal and pluripotency.

functions.name: Convergent evolution of gene expression
functions.description: The independent evolution of similar gene expression patterns in different lineages through distinct molecular mechanisms.

functions.name: Converging transcription of antisense-oriented genes
functions.description: A mechanism contributing to the origin of genic postnatal prepachytene piRNA clusters.

functions.name: coordinated expression with type I IFNs
functions.description: Coordinated expression with type I IFNs indicates that the expression levels of certain genes or elements change in a correlated manner with type I interferons.

functions.name: Copper(I) binding
functions.description: The process by which the ORF1p coiled-coil domain binds copper(I) ions with high affinity.

functions.name: Copy number alterations
functions.description: Changes in the number of copies of a specific genomic region, such as aneuploidies.

functions.name: copy number variation (CNV)
functions.description: Copy number variation is a type of structural variation where the number of copies of a specific DNA segment varies among individuals.

functions.name: Copy number variations
functions.description: Copy number variations are a type of structural variation involving changes in the number of copies of a particular genomic region.

functions.name: Copying by non-HERV machinery
functions.description: Copying by non-HERV machinery is a mechanism where HERV elements are copied by cellular machinery not specific to HERVs.

functions.name: Core decidual regulatory network
functions.description: The core decidual regulatory network is a set of molecular interactions and pathways that govern the decidualization process in endometrial stromal cells.

functions.name: Coretropose
functions.description: Coretropose is the process by which LINE-1 elements mobilize and integrate various non-autonomous RNAs into the genome.

functions.name: Cotranscription
functions.description: Cotranscription refers to the simultaneous transcription of two or more genetic elements from a shared promoter or regulatory region.

functions.name: cotranscriptional splicing
functions.description: Cotranscriptional splicing refers to significant alterations in splicing caused by retroelement insertions.

functions.name: CpA to TpA mutation
functions.description: A specific type of 5-methylcytosine-associated mutation.

functions.name: CpG dinucleotide mutation
functions.description: CpG dinucleotides are hypermutable sites in the genome, often undergoing cytosine methylation and subsequent deamination.

functions.name: CpG DNA methylation
functions.description: CpG DNA methylation is an epigenetic modification primarily occurring at CpG dinucleotides, crucial for silencing transposons.

functions.name: CpG hypomethylation
functions.description: CpG hypomethylation refers to a decrease in the methylation level of cytosine nucleotides in CpG dinucleotide contexts, often associated with genomic instability and altered gene expression.

functions.name: CpG island creation
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposition events lead to the formation of new CpG islands in the genome.

functions.name: CpG island hypermethylation
functions.description: CpG island hypermethylation is an epigenetic modification involving the addition of methyl groups to cytosine residues in CpG-rich regions, often associated with gene silencing.

functions.name: CpG methylation
functions.description: CpG methylation is an epigenetic modification involving the addition of a methyl group to the cytosine nucleotide in a CpG dinucleotide, often associated with gene silencing.

functions.name: CpG methylation in L1 promoter
functions.description: DNA methylation at CpG sites within the promoter region of LINE-1 elements, which regulates their expression.

functions.name: CpG methylation-mediated repression
functions.description: CpG methylation-mediated repression is an epigenetic mechanism that silences gene expression, including that of retrotransposable elements.

functions.name: CpG mutation
functions.description: CpG mutation refers to the high mutation rate of CpG dinucleotides, often resulting in their conversion to TpG or CpA.

functions.name: CpG to TpG mutation
functions.description: A specific type of 5-methylcytosine-associated mutation.

functions.name: CpT to TpT mutation
functions.description: A specific type of 5-methylcytosine-associated mutation.

functions.name: create chimeric transcripts with host genes
functions.description: Creation of chimeric transcripts with host genes refers to the formation of fusion RNAs that include sequences from both a transposable element and a host gene.

functions.name: creating genetic variation
functions.description: Retrotransposons are responsible for creating genetic variation within the human genome.

functions.name: Creation of chimeric retrotranscripts
functions.description: The process of generating fused retrotranscripts, such as U6-L1, using the L1 integration machinery.

functions.name: creation of new exon
functions.description: Creation of a new exon refers to the process by which a DNA sequence is incorporated into a gene's transcript as a coding or non-coding segment.

functions.name: Creation of new microsatellites
functions.description: The creation of new microsatellites is a genomic consequence of L1 insertions.

functions.name: CREB activation
functions.description: Activation of cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB) is a cellular signaling event that can regulate gene expression.

functions.name: CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) silencing
functions.description: A technique using a catalytically dead Cas9 protein to repress gene expression by blocking transcription.

functions.name: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene activation (CRISPRa)
functions.description: CRISPRa is a technique that uses a dCas9 fused to transcriptional activators to upregulate gene expression.

functions.name: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene interference (CRISPRi)
functions.description: CRISPRi is a technique that uses a catalytically dead Cas9 (dCas9) to repress gene expression by blocking transcription.

functions.name: CRISPR/Cas9-induced DSB formation
functions.description: CRISPR/Cas9-induced double-strand break (DSB) formation is a DNA damage mechanism triggered by the CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing tool.

functions.name: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated integration
functions.description: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated integration is a genome editing technique that uses the Cas9 nuclease guided by RNA to create targeted double-strand breaks, enabling precise insertion of DNA sequences.

functions.name: Cryptic exon activation
functions.description: Cryptic exon activation refers to the inclusion of a normally non-coding intronic sequence into a mature mRNA transcript due to the creation of a new splice site.

functions.name: Cryptic exon inclusion
functions.description: Cryptic exon inclusion is a splicing abnormality where a normally non-coding intronic sequence is incorporated into the mature mRNA.

functions.name: Cryptic polyadenylation
functions.description: Cryptic polyadenylation refers to the use of non-canonical or suboptimal polyadenylation signals within a transcript, leading to premature termination of transcription.

functions.name: cryptic promoter activation
functions.description: Cryptic promoter activation is the process by which a normally silent or inactive promoter region becomes transcriptionally active, often due to a genomic alteration.

functions.name: Cryptic promoter activity
functions.description: Cryptic promoter activity refers to the initiation of transcription from sequences not normally functioning as promoters, which can be activated by nearby genomic alterations.

functions.name: Cryptic splice site activation
functions.description: Cryptic splice site activation refers to the unmasking and utilization of normally silent splice sites within introns or exons, often due to mutations.

functions.name: Cryptic splicing variation
functions.description: Cryptic splicing variation refers to alternative splicing events caused by sequence variation within intronic regions, such as VNTRs.

functions.name: CTCF-binding
functions.description: CTCF-binding is a molecular mechanism where the CTCF protein binds to DNA, often involved in chromatin organization and gene regulation.

functions.name: ctDNA integration
functions.description: The process by which circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is inserted into the genome of a recipient cell.

functions.name: cut-and-paste mechanism
functions.description: A transposon-based mechanism involving the excision and reinsertion of genetic material.

functions.name: cut-and-paste transposition
functions.description: A mechanism of transposition where the transposon is excised from its original location and inserted into a new one.

functions.name: Cytidine deamination
functions.description: An enzymatic process that converts cytidine to uridine, which can be a restriction mechanism against retrotransposons.

functions.name: Cytoplasmic accumulation of RNA-DNA hybrids
functions.description: Cytoplasmic accumulation of RNA-DNA hybrids is a process where RNA-DNA hybrid molecules derived from retrotransposons accumulate in the cytoplasm.

functions.name: Cytoplasmic aggregation
functions.description: The formation of protein aggregates in the cytoplasm, a feature of the LINE-1 ORF1p protein.

functions.name: Cytoplasmic DNA accumulation
functions.description: Cytoplasmic DNA accumulation refers to the buildup of DNA, including from active LINE-1 elements, in the cell cytoplasm.

functions.name: Cytoplasmic expression of ORF1p/ORF2p
functions.description: The localization of LINE-1 encoded ORF1p and ORF2p proteins within the cell cytoplasm.

functions.name: Cytoplasmic foci localization
functions.description: Cytoplasmic foci localization is the process where L1-encoded proteins and L1 RNA accumulate in cytoplasmic foci, often associated with stress granules.

functions.name: Cytoplasmic sequestration
functions.description: Cytoplasmic sequestration refers to the process of trapping or confining molecules, such as RNA, in the cytoplasm away from their site of action.

functions.name: cytoplasmic synthesis of Alu complementary DNA
functions.description: The process of reverse transcribing Alu RNA into complementary DNA (cDNA) in the cytoplasm, independently of genomic integration.

functions.name: Cytosine methylation
functions.description: Cytosine methylation is an epigenetic modification involving the addition of a methyl group to cytosine residues in DNA, often associated with gene silencing.

functions.name: Cytosine methylation of L1 promoters
functions.description: A cellular mechanism involving high-density cytosine methylation to downregulate the expression of L1 proteins.

functions.name: cytosolic priming
functions.description: Cytosolic priming refers to the initiation of reverse transcription in the cell cytoplasm, potentially by short RNAs or hairpins.

functions.name: Cytosolic ribonuclease (RNase) degradation
functions.description: Cytosolic ribonuclease degradation is a pathway for degrading LINE-1 RNA, identified as a major regulatory mechanism in the model.

functions.name: Cytotoxicity
functions.description: Cytotoxicity refers to the quality of being toxic to cells, causing cell damage or death.

functions.name: De novo DNA methylation
functions.description: De novo DNA methylation is the process of establishing new DNA methylation marks, often at transposable elements, to repress their transcription.

functions.name: de novo genetic variation
functions.description: De novo genetic variation refers to new genetic changes that arise in an individual's germline or somatic cells and are not inherited from parents.

functions.name: de novo genomic insertions
functions.description: De novo genomic insertions are new insertions of transposable elements into the genome, which can be detected as evidence of retrotransposition activity.

functions.name: De novo insertion
functions.description: De novo insertion refers to the integration of a transposon into a new genomic location.

functions.name: de novo L1 insertion
functions.description: De novo L1 insertion refers to a new insertion event of a LINE-1 element into the genome.

functions.name: de novo L1 integration
functions.description: De novo L1 integration is the process by which a new LINE-1 copy inserts into the genome, initiated by the endonuclease domain nicking a specific DNA sequence.

functions.name: de novo LINE-1 insertion
functions.description: New insertions of LINE-1 elements into the genome, which can potentially drive tumorigenesis.

functions.name: De novo mutation
functions.description: De novo mutation refers to a new genetic alteration that is present for the first time in a family member, caused by an error in DNA replication or repair.

functions.name: De novo repression
functions.description: De novo repression refers to the initial silencing of genetic elements.

functions.name: De novo retrotransposition
functions.description: De novo retrotransposition is the process by which a retrotransposon generates a new genomic insertion through reverse transcription and integration.

functions.name: de novo somatic retrotransposition
functions.description: De novo somatic retrotransposition is a new retrotransposition event occurring in somatic cells of an individual.

functions.name: De novo transposon insertion
functions.description: De novo transposon insertion refers to a new insertion event of a transposon into the genome that was not present in the parental genomes.

functions.name: De-differentiation
functions.description: De-differentiation is a cellular process where specialized cells revert to a less specialized state.

functions.name: De-repression
functions.description: De-repression is the process by which silenced transposable elements become active or accessible.

functions.name: deamination-dependent inhibition
functions.description: Deamination-dependent inhibition is a mechanism of inhibiting LINE-1 retrotransposition that relies on the cytosine deaminase activity of APOBEC3 proteins, leading to cDNA degradation.

functions.name: deamination-independent restriction
functions.description: Deamination-independent restriction is a mechanism of inhibiting LINE-1 retrotransposition that does not rely on the cytosine deaminase activity of APOBEC3 proteins.

functions.name: Decidualization
functions.description: Decidualization is the process of endometrial stromal cell differentiation, a key event in establishing endometrial receptivity for embryo implantation.

functions.name: Decrease of RNA levels
functions.description: Decrease of RNA levels refers to a reduction in the amount of specific RNA transcripts.

functions.name: decreased degradation of L1 DNA or RNA
functions.description: Decreased degradation of L1 DNA or RNA refers to the reduced breakdown of LINE-1 nucleic acids.

functions.name: Decreased gene expression
functions.description: Decreased gene expression refers to a reduction in the level of transcription or translation of a specific gene.

functions.name: Decreased global DNA methylation
functions.description: Decreased global DNA methylation is an epigenetic state characterized by a reduction in the overall level of DNA methylation across the genome.

functions.name: Decreased transcription
functions.description: Decreased transcription refers to a reduction in the rate or level of gene transcription.

functions.name: defending virus infection
functions.description: Defending virus infection is a function where retrotransposons may play a role in the cellular antiviral response.

functions.name: Defense mechanism against transposons
functions.description: A biological process, such as DNA methylation, that suppresses the activity or deleterious effects of transposable elements.

functions.name: defining chromatin TAD and loop boundaries
functions.description: Defining chromatin topologically associating domain (TAD) and loop boundaries refers to the role of sequences in organizing the 3D structure of chromatin.

functions.name: Degradation assessment
functions.description: Degradation assessment is the qualitative measure of the extent of DNA degradation in a sample.

functions.name: degradation of LINE-1 RNA
functions.description: Degradation of LINE-1 RNA is a host control mechanism that reduces the availability of the RNA template required for LINE-1 retrotransposition.

functions.name: Deletion
functions.description: Deletion is the process by which a transposable element is removed from a genomic location.

functions.name: deletion of target genomic DNA
functions.description: The loss of a segment of DNA at the site of an L1 insertion.

functions.name: deletions
functions.description: Deletions are genetic alterations involving the loss of DNA sequences, which can be associated with transposon activity.

functions.name: demethylation
functions.description: Demethylation is the removal of a methyl group from a molecule, such as DNA, which can lead to changes in gene expression.

functions.name: demethylation of repetitive elements
functions.description: Demethylation of repetitive elements, including LINE-1, is a process contributing to genome-wide hypomethylation in cancers.

functions.name: Depletion of mRNA and protein levels
functions.description: Depletion of mRNA and protein levels refers to a significant reduction in the quantity of specific mRNA transcripts and their corresponding proteins.

functions.name: deposition of repressive histone marks
functions.description: Deposition of repressive histone marks is an epigenetic mechanism that leads to gene silencing.

functions.name: deposition of repressive histone modifications
functions.description: The addition of chemical marks to histone proteins that lead to a compact, transcriptionally inactive chromatin state.

functions.name: deregulation of let-7 miRNA expression
functions.description: Deregulation of let-7 miRNA expression refers to abnormal levels or activity of the let-7 microRNA family.

functions.name: derepression in cancer
functions.description: Derepression in cancer refers to the loss of normal silencing mechanisms, leading to the reactivation or increased expression of genes or transposons in cancer cells.

functions.name: Derepression of retrotransposons
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposons, such as LINE-1, are released from transcriptional silencing and become active.

functions.name: Derepression of transposable elements
functions.description: Derepression of transposable elements refers to the loss of normal silencing mechanisms, leading to increased expression and potential activity of these elements.

functions.name: Determination of chronological order and relative ages
functions.description: A method to infer the chronological order and relative ages of human transposable elements spanning over 100 million years based on their insertion/fragmentation patterns.

functions.name: Developmental control
functions.description: Developmental control refers to the regulation of processes that guide the growth and differentiation of an organism from an embryo.

functions.name: developmental plasticity
functions.description: Developmental plasticity is the ability of cells to change their phenotype during development.

functions.name: Developmental program repression
functions.description: The process of suppressing or silencing gene expression programs associated with earlier stages of development.

functions.name: Developmental regulation
functions.description: The control of processes during organism development.

functions.name: developmental reversion
functions.description: Developmental reversion refers to the process where cells revert to an earlier developmental state, such as naive human embryonic stem cells reverting to 8-cell-like cells.

functions.name: developmentally programmed genetic switches
functions.description: Permanent and heritable changes in DNA that control precise gene expression during embryonic development.

functions.name: dGTP-triggered tetramer formation
functions.description: dGTP-triggered tetramer formation is a structural change in the SAMHD1 protein required for its dNTPase activity and LINE-1 regulation.

functions.name: DICER-dependent destruction of L1 mRNAs
functions.description: A cellular mechanism involving DICER to downregulate the expression of L1 proteins by destroying L1 mRNAs.

functions.name: Dicer-mediated RNA interference (RNAi) silencing
functions.description: Dicer-mediated RNA interference (RNAi) silencing is a cellular defense mechanism that uses small interfering RNAs to limit the expansion of retrotransposons.

functions.name: Dicistronic structure
functions.description: A dicistronic structure refers to an mRNA that contains two open reading frames (ORFs) that can be translated into two separate proteins.

functions.name: differential DNA methylation
functions.description: Differential DNA methylation refers to changes in the methylation status of specific genomic loci, which can alter gene expression.

functions.name: Differential expression
functions.description: Differential expression refers to the condition where a gene or element is expressed at different levels between two or more conditions, such as tumor versus healthy tissue.

functions.name: Differential expression of miRNAs
functions.description: Differential expression of miRNAs, such as the let-7 family, involves changes in their levels, which can regulate genes involved in EMT and metastasis.

functions.name: differential expression of proximal genes
functions.description: Differential expression of proximal genes refers to changes in the expression levels of genes located near a genomic locus, such as a retrotransposon.

functions.name: Differential gene expression
functions.description: Differential gene expression refers to changes in the level of gene transcription, as identified in SETMAR knockout cell lines.

functions.name: Differential methylation
functions.description: Differential methylation refers to differences in DNA methylation patterns, such as between alleles or genomic regions.

functions.name: differential transposon insertion
functions.description: The presence or absence of a transposon insertion at a specific genomic locus when comparing two genomes.

functions.name: Differentiation
functions.description: Differentiation is the process by which pluripotent stem cells develop into specialized cell types.

functions.name: Differentiation of sex chromosomes
functions.description: Differentiation of sex chromosomes refers to the evolutionary process where homologous chromosomes (X and Y) accumulate differences and stop recombining over most of their length.

functions.name: differentiation potential
functions.description: Differentiation potential is the ability of a cell to develop into more specialized cell types.

functions.name: Differentiation repression
functions.description: Differentiation repression is a process that maintains pluripotency by inhibiting the transition of stem cells into specialized cell types.

functions.name: Direct occupation
functions.description: Direct occupation refers to transcription factors binding to specific genomic sites, such as LTR sequences.

functions.name: Direct reprogramming
functions.description: Direct reprogramming is a process of converting one cell type directly into another without passing through a pluripotent intermediate state.

functions.name: Disease progression
functions.description: Disease progression refers to the worsening or advancement of a disease over time.

functions.name: disease-causing mutation
functions.description: Retrotransposons are responsible for creating disease-causing mutations within the human genome.

functions.name: Dispersion mechanism
functions.description: The molecular and cellular processes by which transposable elements spread to new genomic locations.

functions.name: disrupt gene function
functions.description: Disruption of gene function refers to the impairment of a gene's normal activity, often through mutation.

functions.name: disruption
functions.description: The interruption or alteration of a genomic sequence or gene function caused by a transposon insertion.

functions.name: Disruption of coding region
functions.description: Disruption of a coding region occurs when a genetic element inserts into an exon, altering the protein-coding sequence.

functions.name: disruption of heterochromatin structure
functions.description: Alteration or destabilization of the condensed, transcriptionally repressive chromatin structure.

functions.name: disruption of mesenchymal to epithelial transition
functions.description: Disruption of mesenchymal to epithelial transition refers to the interference with the cellular process where mesenchymal cells transform into epithelial cells, which is crucial for organogenesis.

functions.name: disruption of nuclear integrity
functions.description: Impairment of the structural and functional integrity of the cell nucleus, including the nuclear envelope.

functions.name: disruption of nucleocytoplasmic transport
functions.description: Impairment of the transport of molecules between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

functions.name: Disruption of open reading frame (ORF)
functions.description: Disruption of the open reading frame (ORF) refers to mutations that prevent the translation of a functional protein from a gene.

functions.name: Distal enhancer activity
functions.description: The function of a non-coding DNA sequence located far from the gene it regulates to increase the transcription of that gene.

functions.name: distal enhancer function
functions.description: A role in regulating gene expression from a distance, typically by looping to interact with gene promoters.

functions.name: distal enhancer regulation
functions.description: The process of controlling gene expression from regulatory elements located far from the gene promoter.

functions.name: disturbance of normal gene expression
functions.description: Disturbance of normal gene expression refers to the abnormal activation or repression of gene transcription, potentially contributing to disease.

functions.name: Divergence-based insertion time estimation
functions.description: A method to estimate the insertion time of an LTR retrotransposon by measuring the sequence divergence between its two LTRs, which were identical at the time of insertion.

functions.name: Diversification
functions.description: Diversification refers to the process by which genomic segments or sequences become more varied over time.

functions.name: Diversification of transcriptional profiles
functions.description: The process of generating variation in the patterns of gene expression across different conditions or cell types.

functions.name: DNA 5-methylcytosine (5mC) methylation
functions.description: DNA 5-methylcytosine (5mC) methylation is an epigenetic modification involved in the silencing of transposable elements.

functions.name: DNA bending and minor groove widening
functions.description: A structural mechanism induced by the βB6-βB5 hairpin loop of L1-Endonuclease, which protrudes into the DNA minor groove, causing bending and widening to position the scissile bond for cleavage.

functions.name: DNA binding
functions.description: DNA binding is the molecular function of proteins or other molecules to attach to specific sequences or structures of DNA.

functions.name: DNA binding site spread
functions.description: The spread of DNA binding sites refers to their distribution across the genome through mechanisms such as transposon mobilization.

functions.name: DNA break repair via homology-dependent pathway
functions.description: A pathway for repairing DNA double-strand breaks that uses a homologous DNA sequence as a template, such as homologous recombination.

functions.name: DNA break repair via nonhomologous end joining
functions.description: A pathway for repairing DNA double-strand breaks by directly ligating the broken ends, often resulting in small insertions or deletions.

functions.name: DNA breaks
functions.description: DNA breaks are physical discontinuities in the DNA backbone, which can be single-strand or double-strand breaks.

functions.name: DNA cleavage
functions.description: DNA cleavage is the enzymatic process of breaking phosphodiester bonds in DNA.

functions.name: DNA cleavage activity
functions.description: DNA cleavage activity refers to the enzymatic ability to cut DNA strands.

functions.name: DNA cleavage by L1 endonuclease
functions.description: DNA cleavage by L1-endonuclease refers to the enzymatic activity of LINE-1 endonuclease that introduces DNA breaks.

functions.name: DNA clustering
functions.description: DNA clustering refers to the phenomenon where specific genome elements are non-randomly grouped together in the genome.

functions.name: DNA crosslink repair
functions.description: DNA crosslink repair is a pathway that resolves interstrand crosslinks, and the Fanconi anemia pathway is a key component of this process.

functions.name: DNA damage

functions.name: Exon skipping

functions.name: Exonic insertion

functions.name: Expansion

functions.name: Expressed single nucleotide variation (SNV)

functions.name: Expression

functions.name: expression of genetic information

functions.name: Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) regulation

functions.name: Expression up-regulation

functions.name: functional diversity between cells

functions.name: Functional genomics

functions.name: functional protein provision

functions.name: fusion transcript formation

functions.name: G4 DNA formation

functions.name: Gain in chromatin accessibility

functions.name: gain of function

functions.name: gene activation

functions.name: Gene activity regulation

functions.name: Gene amplification

functions.name: Gene co-expression modulation

functions.name: gene conversion-mediated deletion

functions.name: Gene correction

functions.name: Gene creation
