functions.name: intraspecific chromosome rearrangement
functions.description: Intraspecific chromosome rearrangement refers to structural changes in chromosomes within a species.

functions.name: Intrastrand tetraplex formation
functions.description: Intrastrand tetraplex formation is a structural feature involving G-rich polypurine tracts that can fold into specific four-stranded DNA structures.

functions.name: Intrinsic immunity
functions.description: Intrinsic immunity refers to the cellular defense mechanisms, such as those mediated by APOBEC proteins, that have evolved to restrict the replication of endogenous retroelements and exogenous retroviruses.

functions.name: Introduce structural variation
functions.description: SINEs contribute to genomic structural changes and variation.

functions.name: introduction of new splice sites
functions.description: Introduction of new splice sites refers to the creation of novel donor or acceptor splice sites within a gene sequence.

functions.name: Introduction of premature termination codons (PTCs)
functions.description: Introduction of premature termination codons (PTCs) is a mechanism that can lead to nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and altered gene function.

functions.name: intron creation
functions.description: Intron creation is the process by which new introns are formed within a gene.

functions.name: Intron expansion
functions.description: Intron expansion refers to the increase in size of an intron over evolutionary time.

functions.name: Intron retention
functions.description: Intron retention is a form of alternative splicing where an intron is not removed from the mature mRNA transcript.

functions.name: Intron size increase
functions.description: Intron size increase refers to the evolutionary process of introns becoming larger, potentially influenced by various mechanisms.

functions.name: intronic enhancer
functions.description: An enhancer element located within an intron of a gene.

functions.name: intronic insertion
functions.description: Intronic insertion refers to the insertion of a DNA sequence into an intron of a gene.

functions.name: Inversion
functions.description: Inversion is a chromosomal rearrangement where a segment of a chromosome is reversed end to end.

functions.name: Inversion of exonic regions
functions.description: Inversion of exonic regions refers to the chromosomal rearrangement that reverses the orientation of exon-containing segments within genes.

functions.name: IRES-mediated translation
functions.description: Internal ribosome entry site (IRES)-mediated translation is a cap-independent mechanism of translation initiation.

functions.name: KAP1 repression
functions.description: KAP1 represses the expression of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) and ZNF genes.

functions.name: KAP1-mediated repression
functions.description: A repression mechanism where KAP1, the master cofactor of KRAB-ZFPs, silences the expression of specific transposon lineages.

functions.name: KRAB/KAP1-induced repression
functions.description: KRAB/KAP1-induced repression is a transcriptional repression system mediated by KRAB-containing zinc finger proteins and their cofactor KAP1.

functions.name: L1 5'-UTR internal promoter activity
functions.description: The transcriptional activity driven by the internal promoter located within the long 5'-untranslated region (5'-UTR) of the human LINE-1 retrotransposon.

functions.name: L1 activation
functions.description: L1 activation refers to the process that enables LINE-1 retrotransposons to become transcriptionally active and capable of retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 activity
functions.description: L1 activity encompasses the processes involved in LINE-1 retrotransposition, including transcription, translation, and the formation of ribonucleoprotein complexes.

functions.name: L1 activity regulation
functions.description: L1 activity regulation refers to the mechanisms by which humans have evolved to limit the activity of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 antisense promoter (ASP) transcriptional activity
functions.description: The antisense promoter (ASP) of L1 elements transcribes L1-gene chimeric RNAs that include neighboring exon sequences.

functions.name: L1 antisense promoter activation
functions.description: L1 antisense promoter (L1-ASP) activation refers to the initiation of transcription from the antisense promoter within the LINE-1 5' UTR.

functions.name: L1 antisense promoter activity
functions.description: The L1 antisense promoter drives transcription of chimeric transcripts, which are 5' L1 antisense sequences spliced to the exons of neighboring genes.

functions.name: L1 antisense RNA expression
functions.description: Transcription from the antisense strand of an L1 retrotransposon.

functions.name: L1 cDNA synthesis
functions.description: L1 cDNA synthesis is the reverse transcription of LINE-1 RNA into complementary DNA, a key step in retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 chimeric transcript (LCT) expression
functions.description: L1 chimeric transcript expression involves the production of transcripts composed of the L1 5' UTR followed by adjacent genomic sequence, initiated by the L1 antisense promoter.

functions.name: L1 chimeric transcript formation
functions.description: L1 chimeric transcript formation refers to the generation of fusion transcripts between LINE-1 sequences and host or viral genes.

functions.name: L1 chimeric transcription
functions.description: The process by which L1 elements express chimeric transcripts.

functions.name: L1 derepression
functions.description: L1 derepression refers to the loss of transcriptional silencing of LINE-1 elements, which can occur under conditions such as DNA hypomethylation.

functions.name: L1 dysregulation
functions.description: L1 dysregulation refers to the abnormal activity or expression of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 element inversion
functions.description: L1 element inversion is a structural alteration where a segment of the L1 element is inserted in the opposite orientation.

functions.name: L1 element-dependent retrotransposition
functions.description: A process of genomic insertion mediated by the reverse transcription and integration of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 endonuclease (L1 EN) activity
functions.description: L1 endonuclease activity is the function of the ORF2 protein that nicks target DNA to initiate reverse transcription.

functions.name: L1 endonuclease cleavage
functions.description: L1 endonuclease cleavage is the process where the L1-encoded endonuclease nicks the target DNA to initiate retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 endonuclease cutting activity
functions.description: L1 endonuclease cutting activity refers to the enzymatic function of the L1-encoded protein that cleaves DNA to initiate target-primed reverse transcription (TPRT) or other DNA rearrangements.

functions.name: L1 endonuclease nicking
functions.description: The process by which the L1 endonuclease cleaves genomic DNA, an important initial step in the L1 transposition reaction.

functions.name: L1 endonuclease-dependent integration
functions.description: An integration mechanism for retrotransposition that depends on the L1 endonuclease activity.

functions.name: L1 endonuclease-mediated de novo insertion
functions.description: A specific mechanism of retrotransposon insertion into the genome that is dependent on the L1 endonuclease activity.

functions.name: L1 endonuclease-mediated retrotransposition
functions.description: The process by which LINE-1 elements, utilizing their encoded endonuclease, insert new copies into the genome.

functions.name: L1 expansion
functions.description: L1 expansion refers to periods of increased activity and genomic insertion of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 expression
functions.description: L1 expression refers to the transcription of LINE-1 elements into RNA.

functions.name: L1 expression during neurogenesis
functions.description: The transcriptional activation of LINE-1 elements, which mimics NeuroD1 gene activation, suggesting a role in neurogenesis.

functions.name: L1 hypomethylation
functions.description: L1 hypomethylation refers to the reduced methylation of LINE-1 elements, often associated with their transcriptional activation.

functions.name: L1 inhibition
functions.description: L1 inhibition refers to the cellular mechanisms that decrease the rate of L1 retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 insert generation
functions.description: The process resulting in the creation of new LINE-1 insertions in the genome.

functions.name: L1 insertion
functions.description: L1 insertion is the process by which a newly synthesized LINE-1 copy integrates into the host genome.

functions.name: L1 insertion polymorphism (LIP)
functions.description: L1 insertion polymorphism refers to the presence or absence of specific L1 retrotransposon insertions in the genome, which varies among individuals.

functions.name: L1 integration
functions.description: The process of L1 retrotransposon insertion into the genome at specific sites.

functions.name: L1 integration machinery
functions.description: The molecular machinery of LINE-1 retrotransposons used for creating new genomic integrations.

functions.name: L1 inversion
functions.description: L1 inversion refers to the creation of inverted and truncated L1 insertions at the 5' end of the element.

functions.name: L1 life cycle
functions.description: The L1 life cycle involves the dynamics of L1 proteins and mRNA localization and function during different stages of the host cell cycle.

functions.name: L1 life cycle regulation
functions.description: L1 life cycle regulation refers to the cellular processes that control the replication and mobilization of LINE-1 retrotransposons.

functions.name: L1 methylation
functions.description: L1 methylation refers to the DNA methylation status of the LINE-1 element, particularly in its 5' untranslated region.

functions.name: L1 mobility
functions.description: L1 mobility refers to the activity and frequency of LINE-1 retrotransposition events.

functions.name: L1 mobilization
functions.description: L1 mobilization refers to the process of LINE-1 retrotransposition and insertion into new genomic locations.

functions.name: L1 mRNA 3' end dynamics
functions.description: L1 mRNA 3' end dynamics refer to the processes affecting the non-templated 3' ends of L1 mRNA, including poly(A) tail length and uridylation, which shape L1 biology and retrotransposition potential.

functions.name: L1 mRNA degradation via autophagy
functions.description: The degradation of LINE-1 RNA transcripts through the cellular autophagy pathway, which is mediated by the m6A reader YTHDF2.

functions.name: L1 mRNA expression
functions.description: L1 mRNA expression is the transcription of LINE-1 elements, which is the first step in retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 mRNA processing
functions.description: L1 mRNA processing involves modifications to the primary LINE-1 transcript, such as splicing.

functions.name: L1 mutagenesis
functions.description: L1 mutagenesis refers to mutations caused by the activity of LINE-1 retrotransposons, such as insertional mutagenesis.

functions.name: L1 ORF1p protein expression
functions.description: L1 ORF1p protein expression is the production of the ORF1 protein from LINE-1 transcripts, commonly detected in human cancers.

functions.name: L1 ORF2 protein translation
functions.description: L1 ORF2 protein translation is the process of synthesizing the ORF2 protein from L1 mRNA, which is essential for L1 retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 ORF2 protein-dependent retrotransposition
functions.description: The retrotransposition of non-autonomous elements like Alu depends on the protein machinery (ORF2p) provided by the autonomous LINE-1 element.

functions.name: L1 ORF2p pausing
functions.description: L1 ORF2p pausing is a molecular mechanism where the L1 ORF2 protein pauses during reverse transcription, potentially leading to truncated insertions of non-autonomous elements like Alu.

functions.name: L1 overexpression
functions.description: An elevated level of L1 mRNA expression compared to normal levels.

functions.name: L1 population dynamics
functions.description: L1 population dynamics refers to the changes in the number and activity of LINE-1 elements within the human population over evolutionary time.

functions.name: L1 proliferation
functions.description: L1 proliferation refers to the replication and spread of LINE-1 elements within the genome.

functions.name: L1 promoter activity
functions.description: L1 promoter activity refers to the transcriptional regulation of the LINE-1 element, which can be induced by various stresses and compounds.

functions.name: L1 promoter demethylation
functions.description: L1 promoter demethylation is the loss of DNA methylation at the promoter region of LINE-1 elements, which can lead to their transcriptional reactivation.

functions.name: L1 promoter hypomethylation
functions.description: Reduced methylation of the L1 promoter, which correlates with increased L1 activity.

functions.name: L1 promoter repression
functions.description: L1 promoter repression is the silencing of the promoter region of LINE-1 elements to prevent their transcription and mobilization.

functions.name: L1 protein expression
functions.description: The production of proteins encoded by the LINE-1 element, which are essential for its retrotransposition activity.

functions.name: L1 protein nuclear entry
functions.description: L1 protein nuclear entry is the process by which L1 proteins enter the nucleus, a necessary step for L1 proliferation.

functions.name: L1 quiescence
functions.description: L1 quiescence refers to periods of low or no activity of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 reactivation

functions.name: L1 regulation
functions.description: L1 regulation involves the cellular mechanisms that control the activity and expression of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 replication
functions.description: L1 replication is the process of self-replication of LINE-1 elements, requiring the proteins ORF1 and ORF2.

functions.name: L1 replication cycle
functions.description: The L1 replication cycle refers to the complete mechanistic process by which LINE-1 elements replicate and mobilize within the genome.

functions.name: L1 repression
functions.description: L1 repression refers to the molecular mechanisms that suppress the transcriptional activity and retrotransposition of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 restriction
functions.description: L1 restriction refers to the process by which host factors, such as APOBEC3 proteins, inhibit the replication of LINE-1 retroelements.

functions.name: L1 retrotransposition activity
functions.description: L1 retrotransposition activity refers to the rate at which LINE-1 elements successfully copy and insert themselves into new genomic locations.

functions.description: The L1 retrotransposition assay is an exogenous cell culture assay used to study the mobilization of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 retrotransposition-induced mutagenesis
functions.description: L1-retrotransposition-induced mutagenesis refers to the generation of mutations caused by the insertion of LINE-1 elements into new genomic locations.

functions.name: L1 retrotransposon activity
functions.description: L1 retrotransposon activity refers to the process of LINE-1 elements mobilizing within the genome via retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 retrotransposon expression

functions.name: L1 retrotransposon insertion
functions.description: L1 retrotransposon insertion refers to the integration of an L1 element into a new genomic location via retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 retrotransposon-induced DNA damage response
functions.description: The cellular response triggered by DNA damage caused by L1 retrotransposition activity.

functions.name: L1 reverse transcriptase activity
functions.description: The enzymatic activity of the LINE-1 ORF2 protein that converts L1 RNA into cDNA during retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 reverse transcription
functions.description: L1 reverse transcription is the process by which the L1 ORF2 protein converts L1 RNA into cDNA.

functions.name: L1 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex formation
functions.description: L1 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex formation is a step in the retrotransposition process, where the L1 RNA and its encoded proteins assemble into a complex.

functions.name: L1 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) formation
functions.description: L1 ribonucleoprotein formation involves the binding of LINE-1-encoded proteins to their encoding transcript, mediating retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 ribonucleoprotein complex integrity
functions.description: The L1 ribonucleoprotein complex is a structure containing L1 RNA and associated proteins, essential for the retrotransposition process.

functions.name: L1 ribonucleoprotein particle (L1-RNP) expression
functions.description: L1-RNP refers to the ribonucleoprotein complex formed by LINE-1 RNA and associated proteins, which is essential for its retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 RNA degradation
functions.description: L1 RNA degradation refers to the cellular process of breaking down LINE-1 RNA, which can inhibit retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 RNA up-regulation
functions.description: L1 RNA up-regulation refers to an increase in the transcription or abundance of LINE-1 RNA.

functions.name: L1 RNA/protein activity

functions.name: L1 RNP complex assembly

functions.name: L1 RNP complex formation
functions.description: The formation of the L1 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex, involving ORF1p and ORF2p proteins bound to L1 RNA, is essential for retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 RNP formation
functions.description: L1 RNP formation is the assembly of LINE-1 RNA and proteins into a ribonucleoprotein complex, which is an essential intermediate for retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 RNP trafficking
functions.description: L1 RNP trafficking refers to the movement of the LINE-1 ribonucleoprotein particle within the cell, particularly towards the nucleus where reverse transcription occurs.

functions.name: L1 RNP translocation
functions.description: L1 RNP translocation refers to the movement of LINE-1 ribonucleoprotein complexes within the host cell.

functions.name: L1 RT activity
functions.description: L1 reverse transcriptase (RT) activity is the enzymatic function required for the reverse transcription step during LINE-1 retrotransposition.

functions.name: L1 silencing
functions.description: L1 silencing refers to the epigenetic repression of LINE-1 retrotransposon expression and activity.

functions.name: L1 structure
functions.description: L1 structure refers to the genomic organization and sequence features of the LINE-1 element.

functions.name: L1 suppression
functions.description: L1 suppression refers to host mechanisms that inhibit or reduce the activity and retrotransposition of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: L1 trans-driven Alu retrotransposition

functions.name: L1 trans-driven retrotransposition

functions.name: L1 trans-driven SVA retrotransposition

functions.name: L1 transcription

functions.name: L1 transcription repression by DNA methylation

functions.name: L1 transcriptional activation

functions.name: L1 transcriptional activity

functions.name: L1 transcriptional regulation

functions.name: L1 transcriptional repression

functions.name: L1 translation

functions.name: L1-induced DNA damage

functions.name: L1-induced mutagenesis

functions.name: L1-initiated mutagenesis

functions.name: L1-mediated Alu retrotransposition

functions.name: L1-mediated gene disruption

functions.name: LINE-1 retrotransposon-mediated insertion

functions.name: LINE-1 RNA degradation

functions.name: LINE-1 RNA transcription

functions.name: LINE-1 transcription

functions.name: LINE-1 transcription initiation

functions.name: LINE-1 transcription regulation

functions.name: LINE-1 transcription upregulation

functions.name: LINE-1 transposition

functions.name: LINE-1-centric chromatin interactions

functions.name: LINE-1-mediated cell toxicity

functions.name: LINE-1-mediated insertion
functions.description: LINE-1-mediated insertion refers to the process where LINE-1 retrotransposition results in the integration of its own or other sequences into new genomic locations.

functions.name: LINE-1-mediated retrotransposition
functions.description: LINE1 mediated retrotransposition is the process by which non-autonomous retrotransposons, such as SVA, are mobilized in the genome via the enzymatic machinery encoded by LINE1 elements.

functions.name: LINE-mediated retrotransposition
functions.description: The process by which LINE retrotransposons facilitate the integration of non-autonomous sequences, such as retroviral mRNA, into the genome.

functions.name: LINE1 suppression
functions.description: LINE1 suppression refers to the inhibition of LINE-1 retrotransposon activity or expression.

functions.name: LINE1 transposition suppression

functions.name: LINE1 upregulation
functions.description: LINE1 upregulation refers to the increased expression of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: LINE1-triggered immune activation
functions.description: LINE1-triggered immune activation refers to the process by which endogenous LINE1 components stimulate the innate immune system.

functions.name: Lineage tracing
functions.description: Lineage tracing is a technique used to track the progeny of a single cell over time to understand cell fate and developmental trajectories.

functions.name: Lineage-specific insertion

functions.name: Lineage-specific protein birth

functions.name: Linkage disequilibrium
functions.description: Linkage disequilibrium is the non-random association of alleles at different loci in a population.

functions.name: Lipid droplet formation
functions.description: Lipid droplet formation is the process of creating intracellular organelles that store neutral lipids.

functions.name: liquid droplet formation
functions.description: A biophysical process associated with phase separation, leading to the formation of membrane-less organelles or compartments.

functions.name: liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS)
functions.description: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) is a biophysical process where biomolecules condense into membrane-less compartments, facilitating specific cellular functions.

functions.name: lncRNA expression

functions.name: Local adaptation

functions.name: local immune evasion

functions.name: local regulation
functions.description: Local regulation refers to the control of gene or element expression by nearby sequence contexts or factors, as opposed to global regulation.

functions.name: Locus protection from integration

functions.name: locus-specific transcriptional regulation

functions.name: long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) expression

functions.name: Long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) function

functions.name: long-range enhancer-promoter chromatin interactions

functions.name: Long-range promoter-enhancer interaction

functions.name: Long-range transcriptional regulation

functions.name: Long-term gene expression

functions.name: Loop formation

functions.name: Loss of 5mC methylation

functions.name: Loss of DNA cytosine methylation

functions.name: Loss of efficient DNA repair

functions.name: loss of genome stability
functions.description: Loss of genome stability refers to the increased rate of genomic alterations, including mutations and chromosomal changes.

functions.name: loss of heterochromatin

functions.name: loss of methylation

functions.name: LTR-driven gene expression

functions.name: LTR-mediated retroposition

functions.name: M1 macrophage polarization

functions.name: m6A methylation

functions.name: Maintaining genome integrity

functions.name: maintaining memory function
functions.description: Maintaining memory function refers to preserving the ability of CAR-T cells to persist and respond effectively after administration.

functions.name: maintaining pluripotency
functions.description: Maintaining pluripotency refers to the process of keeping embryonic stem cells in an undifferentiated state with the potential to develop into any cell type.

functions.name: Maintaining trans-generational genome stability
functions.description: Maintaining trans-generational genome stability refers to the preservation of genomic integrity across generations.

functions.name: Maintenance of H3K27me3 levels
functions.description: Maintenance of H3K27me3 levels refers to the process of sustaining repressive histone modifications, particularly at specific genomic loci.

functions.name: Maintenance of neuronal progenitor cells
functions.description: Maintenance of neuronal progenitor cells refers to the biological processes that keep these stem-like cells in an undifferentiated, proliferative state.

functions.name: Maintenance of retrotransposons
functions.description: Maintenance of retrotransposons refers to the processes that sustain the presence and activity of retrotransposons within a genome over evolutionary time.

functions.name: malignant progression
functions.description: Malignant progression refers to the development of more aggressive and invasive cancer phenotypes.

functions.name: malignant transformation

functions.name: Malignization

functions.name: Mammalian evolution

functions.name: Mammalian-specific genomic functions

functions.name: mcr restriction

functions.name: MDA5-mediated LINE-1 suppression

functions.name: Mechano-response enhancer element (MREE) activity
functions.description: The function of transposable elements to act as enhancers that respond to mechanical cues from the cellular microenvironment.

functions.name: Mediating chromosome rearrangements
functions.description: Mediating chromosome rearrangements involves processes that lead to structural changes in chromosomes.

functions.name: mediating epigenetic memory
functions.description: Mediating epigenetic memory is a function where retrotransposons can contribute to the maintenance of epigenetic states across cell divisions.

functions.name: Mediating homeology-driven DNA recombination or repair

functions.name: Mediating homology-driven DNA recombination or repair
functions.description: A mechanism where transposable elements facilitate DNA recombination or repair based on sequence homology.

functions.name: Mediating microhomology-driven DNA recombination or repair
functions.description: A mechanism where transposable elements facilitate DNA recombination or repair based on short stretches of sequence similarity (microhomology).

functions.name: memory formation

functions.name: metabolic reprogramming

functions.name: metastasis

functions.name: methylation

functions.name: Methylation quantitative trait loci (mQTL)

functions.name: Microhomology end-joining

functions.name: Microhomology-driven single-strand annealing

functions.name: microhomology-mediated mispairing

functions.name: Microhomology-mediated repair

functions.name: micronuclei formation

functions.name: microRNA (miRNA) regulation

functions.name: microsatellite generation

functions.name: miRNA duplication

functions.name: miRNA gene emergence

functions.name: Mis-expression

functions.name: Misregulation of retrotransposons

functions.name: MITE mobilization

functions.name: mitochondrial dysfunction

functions.name: Mitotic potential

functions.name: Mobile element insertion

functions.name: mobile regulatory element

functions.name: mobility

functions.name: Mobilization

functions.name: Mobilization efficiency determination

functions.name: Mobilization of transposable elements

functions.name: Modification of chromatin structure and function

functions.name: modification of gene expression
functions.description: Modification of gene expression refers to changes in the level or timing of gene activity.

functions.name: modification of transcribed coding sequence

functions.name: modifications in gene expression

functions.name: Modify gene regulatory networks

functions.name: Modulating gene activity

functions.name: Modulation of apoptotic responses

functions.name: modulation of cellular plasticity
functions.description: Modulation of cellular plasticity refers to the influence on a cell's ability to change its phenotype or state.

functions.name: Modulation of DNA methylation

functions.name: Modulation of gene expression

functions.name: mRNA splicing modulation

functions.name: myoblast proliferation

functions.name: ncRNA biogenesis

functions.name: neural differentiation

functions.name: Neuroinflammation

functions.name: Neuronal development
