functions.description: Transcription by RNA polymerase II, which transcribes Alu RNAs embedded within coding or noncoding RNA transcripts.

functions.name: Pol II transcription complex assembly
functions.description: The assembly of RNA polymerase II and associated factors at a promoter to initiate transcription.

functions.name: Pol II-binding aptamer (RAP) activity
functions.description: Pol II-binding aptamer (RAP) activity refers to the ability of specific RNA sequences to bind RNA polymerase II.

functions.name: Pol III transcription
functions.description: Transcription by RNA polymerase III, which transcribes free Alu RNAs.

functions.name: Poly(A) binding protein (PABP) interaction
functions.description: The interaction between the A-rich region of SINE RNAs and the poly(A) binding protein (PABP).

functions.name: Poly(A) microsatellite formation
functions.description: Poly(A) microsatellite formation refers to the concurrent creation of a poly(A) DNA tract at the 3'-end of a retrotransposon insertion, which serves as the origin for a new microsatellite.

functions.name: Poly(A) tail dynamics
functions.description: Poly(A) tail dynamics refer to the processes regulating the length and integrity of the polyadenylate tail at the 3' end of retrotransposon transcripts, which can influence their stability and retrotransposition efficiency.

functions.name: Poly(A) tail length-dependent mobility
functions.description: The rate of Alu retrotransposition varies significantly depending on the length of its poly(A) tail.

functions.name: Polyadenylation
functions.description: Polyadenylation is the addition of a poly(A) tail to the 3' end of an RNA transcript, often involved in its maturation and stability.

functions.name: Polyadenylation at the 3' end
functions.description: A process involving conserved cis-acting elements (hexamer, cleavage site, GU-rich region) for adding a polyA tail to the 3' end of LINE-1 elements.

functions.name: Polyadenylation bypass
functions.description: Polyadenylation bypass is a process where L1 mRNAs sometimes bypass their own polyadenylation signal and use fortuitous signals in flanking genomic DNA.

functions.name: Polyadenylation function
functions.description: Polyadenylation function refers to the ability of a DNA sequence, such as an LTR, to signal the addition of a poly(A) tail to an RNA transcript.

functions.name: Polymerization of ORF1p
functions.description: The process by which human L1 ORF1p forms polymers under low-salt conditions in the absence of nucleic acids.

functions.name: polymorphic insertion
functions.description: Polymorphic insertion refers to the presence of a transposable element at a specific genomic location in some individuals but not others.

functions.name: polymorphic mobile element insertion (pMEI)
functions.description: Polymorphic mobile element insertion (pMEI) is a type of genomic variation caused by the insertion of a mobile element that is not present in all individuals of a species.

functions.name: Polymorphic SVA insertion
functions.description: Polymorphic SVA insertion refers to SVA insertions that vary between individuals, contributing to genomic variation.

functions.name: Polymorphic TE insertion
functions.description: Polymorphic TE insertion refers to a transposable element insertion that is present in some individuals and absent in others, creating genetic variation.

functions.name: polymorphic TE insertions
functions.description: Polymorphic TE insertions are transposable element insertions that vary among individuals in a population.

functions.name: Polymorphic transposable element insertion
functions.description: Polymorphic transposable element insertion refers to the presence of a transposon at a specific genomic locus that varies among individuals in a population.

functions.name: Polymorphism
functions.description: Polymorphism refers to the presence of multiple sequence variants at a specific genomic locus in a population.

functions.name: Population evolution analysis
functions.description: Population evolution analysis is the study of genetic variation and changes in allele frequencies within and between populations over time.

functions.name: Population genetic marker
functions.description: A population genetic marker is a genetic variant used to study the genetic structure, history, and diversity of populations.

functions.name: Population subdivision
functions.description: Population subdivision refers to the division of a large population into smaller, reproductively isolated subpopulations (demes).

functions.name: Pose risk to genome integrity
functions.description: The potential of retrotransposons to cause harmful genomic instability through their activity.

functions.name: positioning changes
functions.description: Positioning changes refer to alterations in the genomic location or nucleosome positioning of transposons over evolutionary time.

functions.name: Positive feedback loop
functions.description: A positive feedback loop is a state where increased LINE-1 activity leads to exponential growth in cDNA copy number, as predicted by the computational model.

functions.name: Positive selection
functions.description: Positive selection is a form of natural selection that increases the frequency of a beneficial allele in a population.

functions.name: Post-insertion selection
functions.description: The process of natural selection acting on transposon copies after their integration into the genome.

functions.name: post-insertion-based mutagenesis
functions.description: Post-insertion-based mutagenesis refers to genomic rearrangements caused by transposons after their initial insertion, such as through non-allelic homologous recombination.

functions.name: Post-insertional genomic injury
functions.description: Genomic damage occurring after the insertion of a retroelement, potentially through mechanisms like ectopic recombination.

functions.name: Post-transcriptional defense
functions.description: Post-transcriptional defense mechanisms suppress transposable element activity after transcription, such as through RNA interference.

functions.name: Post-transcriptional gene regulation
functions.description: Post-transcriptional gene regulation refers to the control of gene expression after the RNA transcript has been made.

functions.name: post-transcriptional modification
functions.description: Post-transcriptional modification refers to changes made to RNA molecules after transcription, which can be influenced by transposable element sequences.

functions.name: Post-transcriptional regulation
functions.description: Post-transcriptional regulation involves processes that control RNA metabolism after transcription, such as modification, stability, and translation.

functions.name: Post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression
functions.description: Post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression involves mechanisms that control gene expression after transcription has occurred.

functions.name: post-transcriptional repression
functions.description: Post-transcriptional repression refers to the regulation of gene or transposon expression after transcription has occurred, often through RNA degradation or translational inhibition.

functions.name: Post-translational regulation
functions.description: Post-translational regulation refers to the control of protein activity or stability after translation.

functions.name: Post-translational regulation of L1 activity
functions.description: Post-translational regulation of L1 activity refers to the potential control of LINE-1 function through modifications after protein synthesis.

functions.name: Post-translational regulation of retrotransposition
functions.description: Post-translational regulation of retrotransposition refers to cellular mechanisms that control L1 activity after the L1 proteins have been synthesized.

functions.name: POU1F1-dependent activation
functions.description: POU1F1-dependent activation is the process by which the transcription factor POU1F1 (Pit-1) stimulates gene expression.

functions.name: Precise deletion
functions.description: Precise deletion refers to the exact removal of a previously established retrotransposon insertion.

functions.name: precise excision
functions.description: Precise excision refers to the removal of a transposon from its insertion site without leaving 'footprint' mutations.

functions.name: Precise parallel insertion
functions.description: Precise parallel insertion refers to the independent insertion of apparently identical retrotransposons at orthologous positions in different lineages.

functions.name: Precise transposon excision
functions.description: Precise transposon excision is the clean removal of a transposon from its original genomic location during transposition.

functions.name: Predisposing to genomic instability
functions.description: The action of increasing the susceptibility of a genomic region to structural changes or mutations.

functions.name: preimplantation development
functions.description: Preimplantation development refers to the early embryonic stages from fertilization to implantation.

functions.name: Preimplantation embryo development
functions.description: Preimplantation embryo development refers to the early stages of embryonic development before implantation in the uterus.

functions.name: Preintegration barrier
functions.description: A barrier that prevents L1 retrotransposition before its integration into the genome.

functions.name: Premature insertion mechanism
functions.description: Premature insertion mechanism refers to the process where a transposon insertion event is terminated before completion, often resulting in truncated sequences.

functions.name: premature polyadenylation
functions.description: Premature polyadenylation is a mechanism that down-regulates gene expression by adding a poly(A) tail early.

functions.name: Premature stop codon creation
functions.description: Premature stop codon creation is a mutation that introduces a stop codon within the coding sequence, leading to truncated protein production.

functions.name: Premature stop codon introduction
functions.description: Premature stop codon introduction is a molecular consequence where a mutation or aberrant splicing creates a stop codon earlier than the normal termination site, leading to a truncated protein.

functions.name: Premature termination codon introduction
functions.description: Premature termination codon introduction is the creation of a stop codon within the coding sequence, leading to truncated protein products.

functions.name: preservation of genome integrity
functions.description: This is a cellular function aimed at maintaining the stability and fidelity of the genome, preventing mutations and structural variations.

functions.name: Preservation of naive pluripotency
functions.description: The maintenance of the earliest, most primitive state of pluripotency in stem cells.

functions.name: Prevention of developmental reversion
functions.description: Prevention of developmental reversion refers to the mechanism that blocks the reversion of naive human embryonic stem cells to an earlier developmental state, such as 8-cell-like cells.

functions.name: Primate identification
functions.description: The process of determining the primate species from which a DNA sample or tissue originated.

functions.name: Pro-inflammatory cytokine production
functions.description: Pro-inflammatory cytokine production is the synthesis of signaling molecules that promote inflammation.

functions.name: Pro-oncogenic perturbation
functions.description: Pro-oncogenic perturbation refers to genomic alterations that promote the initiation or progression of cancer.

functions.name: pro-tumorigenic inflammation
functions.description: Pro-tumorigenic inflammation refers to chronic, tumor-promoting inflammatory responses within the tumor microenvironment.

functions.name: processed pseudogene formation
functions.description: Processed pseudogene formation occurs when LINE-1 retrotransposes cellular mRNAs.

functions.name: Processed pseudogene generation
functions.description: Processed pseudogene generation is a mechanism where host messenger RNA is reverse-transcribed and integrated into the genome, creating a non-functional copy of a gene.

functions.name: Processed pseudogene genesis
functions.description: The process by which processed pseudogenes are generated through retrotransposition of mRNA transcripts.

functions.name: processive DNA polymerization
functions.description: Processive DNA polymerization is the ability of a polymerase to add multiple nucleotides to a growing DNA chain without dissociating from the template.

functions.name: Processive DNA synthesis
functions.description: Processive DNA synthesis describes the ability of a polymerase to incorporate many nucleotides without dissociating from the template; L1 RT is shown to be highly processive.

functions.name: Programmed cell death
functions.description: Programmed cell death is a regulated process of cell suicide, often indicated by increased levels of cleaved caspase-3.

functions.name: Promoter acquisition
functions.description: Promoter acquisition is the process by which a gene or retroelement gains regulatory sequences to enable its transcription.

functions.name: promoter activity
functions.description: The function of a DNA sequence in initiating transcription of a particular gene.

functions.name: Promoter activity in vivo
functions.description: L1 ASP can act as a promoter in living organisms.

functions.name: Promoter activity modulation by flanking sequence
functions.description: The process by which upstream flanking cellular sequences strongly influence the L1 5'-UTR promoter activity, either repressing or enhancing it.

functions.name: Promoter activity of LINE-1 5' UTR
functions.description: The promoter activity of the LINE-1 5' untranslated region (UTR) drives the transcription of LINE-1 RNA, which is the first step in the retrotransposition cycle.

functions.name: Promoter activity regulation
functions.description: The process of controlling the level of transcription initiation from a gene promoter.

functions.name: Promoter activity regulation of LINE-1 5'-UTR
functions.description: Promoter activity regulation of LINE-1 5'-UTR refers to the control of transcription initiation from the internal promoter located within the 5' untranslated region of LINE-1.

functions.name: Promoter and first exon function
functions.description: The process by which a transposon element functions as the promoter and first exon of a protein-coding gene.

functions.name: Promoter binding
functions.description: The process where a transcription factor binds to gene promoter regions to regulate transcription.

functions.name: Promoter blocking
functions.description: Promoter blocking refers to the inhibition of transcriptional activity from a gene or element's promoter region.

functions.name: Promoter capture
functions.description: Promoter capture is a mechanism by which transposable elements acquire and utilize host gene promoters to drive their own expression.

functions.name: Promoter creation
functions.description: Promoter creation refers to the formation of novel transcriptional start sites.

functions.name: Promoter divergence
functions.description: The process by which the regulatory regions of duplicate genes become functionally distinct.

functions.name: promoter DNA demethylation
functions.description: Promoter DNA demethylation is the removal of methyl groups from cytosine residues in gene promoter regions, often associated with gene activation.

functions.name: Promoter DNA methylation
functions.description: Promoter DNA methylation is an epigenetic modification that typically represses gene or transposon expression.

functions.name: Promoter function
functions.description: Promoter function refers to the ability of a DNA sequence to initiate transcription of a gene.

functions.name: promoter hypomethylation
functions.description: Promoter hypomethylation is a reduction in DNA methylation at promoter regions, often associated with increased gene expression.

functions.name: promoter interaction
functions.description: Promoter interaction refers to the physical association between an enhancer and a gene promoter to regulate transcription.

functions.name: Promoter methylation
functions.description: Promoter methylation is an epigenetic modification that typically leads to gene silencing by inhibiting transcription factor binding.

functions.name: Promoter recruitment
functions.description: The process by which a transposable element is independently co-opted to serve as an alternative promoter for gene expression.

functions.name: promoter/enhancer activity
functions.description: Promoter/enhancer activity refers to the ability of a DNA sequence to initiate or increase the transcription of a gene.

functions.name: Promoting cancer cell invasion and metastasis
functions.description: The process by which cancer cells acquire the ability to invade surrounding tissues and spread to distant sites.

functions.name: promoting cellular plasticity
functions.description: Enhancing a cell's ability to change its state, such as during differentiation or in response to environmental cues.

functions.name: promoting cellular senescence
functions.description: A pleiotropic effect induced by L1 transposons.

functions.name: promoting genome instability
functions.description: A pleiotropic effect induced by L1 transposons.

functions.name: promoting inflammation
functions.description: A pleiotropic effect induced by L1 transposons.

functions.name: promotion of cell proliferation
functions.description: Promotion of cell proliferation is a biological process where L1ORF1p overexpression enhances cell growth and colony formation.

functions.name: Promotion of LINE-1 retrotransposition
functions.description: The process of increasing the rate or activity of LINE-1 retrotransposition.

functions.name: propagation
functions.description: Propagation refers to the successful replication and spread of transposable elements within a genome.

functions.name: protein aggregation
functions.description: Protein aggregation is the process where misfolded or unfolded proteins clump together, often leading to loss of function or toxicity.

functions.name: Protein evolution
functions.description: Protein evolution refers to the process by which changes in protein structure or function arise, often through genetic alterations.

functions.name: protein expression
functions.description: Protein expression refers to the production of proteins from their corresponding genes.

functions.name: protein interaction
functions.description: Protein interaction refers to the physical or functional association between proteins.

functions.name: Protein multimerization
functions.description: Protein multimerization is the process by which multiple protein subunits assemble into a larger complex.

functions.name: protein synthesis stimulation
functions.description: Protein synthesis stimulation refers to the enhancement of the process by which cells build proteins.

functions.name: Protein truncation
functions.description: Protein truncation is the production of a shortened, often non-functional, protein product.

functions.name: Protein-coding gene evolution
functions.description: The process through which LTRs contribute to the creation of new protein-coding genes by providing regulatory and coding sequences.

functions.name: Protein-coding region formation
functions.description: The process by which repeat sequences become functional elements, such as protein-coding regions.

functions.name: Protein-protein interaction
functions.description: Protein-protein interaction is the physical association between two or more protein molecules.

functions.name: Protein-protein interaction screening
functions.description: A method to systematically identify proteins that physically interact with a protein of interest.

functions.name: Providing a fragile site for double-strand breaks
functions.description: Providing a fragile site for double-strand breaks refers to creating genomic locations that are prone to DNA double-strand breaks.

functions.name: Providing accessible chromatin regions
functions.description: The function of contributing to genomic regions that are open and accessible for transcription factor binding and gene regulation.

functions.name: providing alternative promoters
functions.description: Providing alternative promoters refers to a transposon insertion creating new transcription start sites for a gene.

functions.name: Providing breakpoints
functions.description: Providing breakpoints refers to the role of a sequence in facilitating genomic rearrangements by serving as a site for DNA breakage and rejoining.

functions.name: Providing complete exon cassettes
functions.description: The contribution of sequences that constitute entire, functional exons.

functions.name: Providing novel promoters
functions.description: The process by which transposable elements supply new promoter regions to host genes upon integration.

functions.name: Providing novel splicing sites
functions.description: The process by which transposable elements introduce new splice donor or acceptor sites into host genes upon integration.

functions.name: providing polyadenylation signals
functions.description: Providing polyadenylation signals is a mechanism by which retroelements interfere with gene expression.

functions.name: Providing promoters
functions.description: The contribution of regulatory sequences that initiate transcription of a gene.

functions.name: providing regulatory modules
functions.description: Providing regulatory modules is a mechanism where retrotransposons can influence gene expression by supplying enhancers, silencers, or other regulatory elements.

functions.name: Providing splice donors and acceptors
functions.description: The contribution of sequences that define the boundaries of introns for splicing.

functions.name: Providing stop codon and polyadenylation signal
functions.description: A process where a genetic element contributes sequences that signal the termination of translation (stop codon) and the addition of a poly(A) tail to mRNA (polyadenylation signal).

functions.name: Providing terminal exons
functions.description: The contribution of sequences that form the final exon of a transcript, often containing the stop codon and polyadenylation signal.

functions.name: Providing transcription termination sites
functions.description: The act of supplying genomic sequences that serve as signals for the termination of transcription.

functions.name: Proviral integration
functions.description: Proviral integration is the process by which a retroviral DNA copy is inserted into the host genome.

functions.name: Provision of mRNA splicing signals
functions.description: Provision of mRNA splicing signals refers to the supply of sequences that guide the removal of introns and joining of exons in pre-mRNA.

functions.name: Provision of promoters and regulatory sequences
functions.description: Provision of promoters and regulatory sequences refers to the contribution of genetic elements that control the initiation and regulation of gene transcription.

functions.name: Provision of STOP codons
functions.description: Provision of STOP codons refers to the introduction of nucleotide triplets that signal the termination of protein synthesis.

functions.name: Provision of transcription initiation signals
functions.description: Provision of transcription initiation signals refers to the supply of sequences that mark the start site for RNA synthesis.

functions.name: Pseudoexon insertion
functions.description: Pseudoexon insertion is the incorporation of a cryptic or non-canonical exon into a mature mRNA transcript.

functions.name: Pseudogene creation
functions.description: The generation of non-functional copies of genes through retrotransposition.

functions.name: Pseudogene formation
functions.description: Pseudogene formation is a process where non-functional copies of genes are generated, in this case mediated by L1 reverse transcriptase activity.

functions.name: Pseudogenization
functions.description: Pseudogenization is the process by which a functional gene loses its protein-coding ability, often due to mutations.

functions.name: Purifying selection
functions.description: Purifying selection is a type of natural selection that acts to remove deleterious genetic variants from a population.

functions.name: purinergic signaling
functions.description: Purinergic signaling involves the extracellular actions of purine nucleotides and nucleosides, such as ATP and adenosine, on cell surface receptors.

functions.name: Purkinje cell degeneration
functions.description: Purkinje cell degeneration is the loss of Purkinje neurons in the cerebellum, a key pathological feature in several ataxias.

functions.name: Quantification
functions.description: Quantification refers to the measurement of the amount or concentration of a specific target, such as human-derived cfDNA, in a biological sample.

functions.name: R-loop formation
functions.description: The formation of RNA-DNA hybrids, which are key intermediates during LINE-1 retrotransposition, including cis L1 R-loops (L1 mRNA-genomic DNA) and trans L1 R-loops (L1 mRNA-complementary DNA).

functions.name: Random insertion
functions.description: Random insertion refers to the distribution pattern of recent L1 insertions in genomic DNA.

functions.name: random reinsertion
functions.description: Random reinsertion refers to the process where retrotransposons insert into new genomic locations in a non-targeted manner.

functions.name: Randomized mutagenesis
functions.description: Randomized mutagenesis is a technique for introducing random mutations at a specific genomic locus to study protein function, regulatory elements, or model genetic variations.

functions.name: Rapid evolution
functions.description: A high rate of sequence change over evolutionary time, characteristic of certain genomic elements.

functions.name: rapid folding
functions.description: Rapid folding is the process by which a protein quickly attains its native three-dimensional structure to avoid misfolding or aggregation.

functions.name: RBP association
functions.description: The binding of RNA Binding Proteins to specific sequences within RNA transcripts, influencing their fate and function.

functions.name: reactivation
functions.description: Reactivation refers to the process by which previously silenced genetic elements become transcriptionally active again.

functions.name: Reactivation of embryonic transcription profiles
functions.description: Reactivation of embryonic transcription profiles refers to the re-expression of gene expression patterns characteristic of embryonic development.

functions.name: reactivation of transposable elements
functions.description: Reactivation of transposable elements refers to the process where silenced transposable elements become transcriptionally active again.

functions.name: readthrough transcription
functions.description: Transcription that continues beyond the normal termination signal of a gene, potentially producing a chimeric transcript.

functions.name: Rearrangement
functions.description: Rearrangement refers to structural changes in the genome, such as deletions, duplications, inversions, or translocations.

functions.name: recapture
functions.description: The process by which host defense proteins evolve to recognize and silence transposons that had previously evaded them.

functions.name: Recent transposition
functions.description: Recent transposition refers to the movement of a transposable element within the genome that has occurred in the recent evolutionary past.

functions.name: Receptor for insertion
functions.description: A receptor for insertion is a genomic site or sequence that serves as a target for the integration of other transposons.

functions.name: Reciprocal regulation
functions.description: Reciprocal regulation describes a mutual regulatory relationship between two or more molecular entities, such as between LINE-1 and transcription factors.

functions.name: Reciprocal regulatory influence
functions.description: The reciprocal regulatory influence refers to the bidirectional interaction between individual L1 copies and their genomic integration sites.

functions.name: reciprocal translocations
functions.description: Reciprocal translocations are structural chromosomal rearrangements involving the exchange of segments between non-homologous chromosomes.

functions.name: recombination
functions.description: Recombination is a mechanism of genome alteration created by retrotransposable elements.

functions.name: recombination between retrotransposons
functions.description: Recombination between retrotransposons is an event where increased copy numbers provide more chances for recombination, potentially leading to chromosomal breaks.

functions.name: Recombination cold spot
functions.description: A recombination cold spot is a genomic region where the frequency of meiotic recombination is significantly lower than the genome average.

functions.name: recombination mechanisms
functions.description: Genetic processes that rearrange DNA sequences, related to mobile element activity.

functions.name: recombination of L1 insertion intermediates
functions.description: Recombination of L1 insertion intermediates refers to the process where the DNA intermediates generated during LINE-1 retrotransposition interact with other DNA breaks or with each other to form new genomic junctions.

functions.name: recombination-associated genomic deletion
functions.description: Recombination-associated genomic deletion is a mechanism where recombination events involving transposable elements result in the loss of genomic material.

functions.name: recombination-based mechanisms
functions.description: Recombination-based mechanisms are processes that use DNA recombination to maintain or elongate telomeres, often as an alternative to telomerase.

functions.name: Recombination-mediated integration
functions.description: Recombination-mediated integration is a mechanism for the insertion of genetic material, such as a circular intermediate, into the genome.

functions.name: Recombinational editing
functions.description: A proposed mechanism for the nonrandom genomic distribution of transposons involving recombination events.

functions.name: Recruitment of transcription factors
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposons bind and attract specific transcription factors.

functions.name: Recruitment of transcriptional repressors
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposons bind and attract proteins that suppress gene transcription.

functions.name: Reduced gene expression
functions.description: Reduced gene expression refers to a decrease in the level of transcription or translation of a specific gene.

functions.name: Reduced primary transcript content
functions.description: Decreased content of the corresponding hnRNAs (heterogeneous nuclear RNAs) due to specific transposon insertions.

functions.name: redundant silencing pathways
functions.description: Redundant silencing pathways are mechanisms that can repress L1 expression even in the absence of DNA methylation.

functions.name: Regenerative therapy
functions.description: Regenerative therapy involves the use of cells, genes, or biomaterials to repair, replace, or regenerate damaged tissues or organs.

functions.name: regional gene regulation
functions.description: The regulation of genes in a spatially defined manner within genomic regions such as TADs.

functions.name: Regional mutation pressure
functions.description: Regional mutation pressure refers to the tendency for repetitive sequences to be subject to the same mutation pressure as their surrounding genomic regions, leading to similar GC content.

functions.name: Regional silencing
functions.description: Regional silencing is a mechanism where gene or transposon repression occurs preferentially over a defined chromosomal region rather than genome-wide.

functions.name: regulated transcriptional expression
functions.description: Regulated transcriptional expression refers to the controlled transcription of genetic elements.

functions.name: regulating cell fate
functions.description: Regulating cell fate is a function where retrotransposons can influence the developmental potential or differentiation state of a cell.

functions.name: Regulating cell interactions during inflammatory reaction
functions.description: A biological process involving the control of communication and responses between cells in the context of inflammation.

functions.name: Regulating gene expression
functions.description: Regulating gene expression is the process of controlling the amount and timing of gene product production.

functions.name: regulating gene expression posttranscriptionally
functions.description: Regulating gene expression posttranscriptionally is a function where retrotransposons can influence RNA processing, stability, or translation.

functions.name: regulating nearby genes
functions.description: Regulating nearby genes is a function where retrotransposons can influence the expression of endogenous genes located in their vicinity.

functions.name: regulation
functions.description: The activity of transposable elements is tightly regulated by genetic and epigenetic mechanisms.

functions.name: Regulation by DNA methylation
functions.description: Regulation by DNA methylation refers to the control of gene or repeat expression through the addition of methyl groups to cytosine bases in DNA.

functions.name: Regulation during early embryonic development
functions.description: Regulation during early embryonic development refers to the control of retrotransposon expression and activity in the context of early embryogenesis.

functions.name: Regulation in inflammatory settings
functions.description: The control of LTR retrotransposon expression levels in the context of inflammation.

functions.name: regulation of chromatin landscapes
functions.description: Regulation of chromatin landscapes refers to the control of chromatin structure and accessibility, which influences gene expression.

functions.name: regulation of DNA transposon activity
functions.description: The process of controlling the mobilization and insertion frequency of DNA transposons.

functions.name: Regulation of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL)
functions.description: The process by which genetic variants influence the expression levels of genes or other transcripts.

functions.name: Regulation of gene expression
functions.description: Regulation of gene expression is the process by which the amount or activity of a gene product is controlled.

functions.name: Regulation of gene expression in immune response
functions.description: The process by which gene expression is controlled during the immune response to infection.

functions.name: regulation of genome structure
functions.description: The process of influencing the organization and architecture of the genome.

functions.name: Regulation of human genes
functions.description: Regulation of human genes refers to the control of gene expression, which can be influenced by nearby genomic elements like ERVs/LRs.

functions.name: regulation of immune-inflammatory responses
functions.description: The regulation of immune-inflammatory responses involves controlling the body's defense mechanisms against pathogens and tissue damage.

functions.name: regulation of nephrogenesis
functions.description: Regulation of nephrogenesis involves the control of kidney development and the formation of nephrons.

functions.name: Regulation of pluripotency states
functions.description: Regulation of pluripotency states refers to the molecular control of distinct pluripotent cell states.

functions.name: Regulation of protein-coding gene expression
functions.description: The process by which SINE retrotransposons impact the expression of protein-coding genes.

functions.name: Regulation of retrotransposable elements
functions.description: Regulation of retrotransposable elements refers to the cellular mechanisms that control the expression and activity of retrotransposons.

functions.name: Regulation of retrotransposition
functions.description: Regulation of retrotransposition refers to the cellular mechanisms that control the frequency and activity of LINE-1 retrotransposition events.

functions.name: Regulation of retrotransposons
functions.description: Regulation of retrotransposons involves cellular silencing mechanisms that restrict the expression and mobility of retrotransposable elements to prevent genomic damage.

functions.name: Regulation of stochastic fluctuations
functions.description: Regulation of stochastic fluctuations refers to the control of random variations in the copy numbers of transposable elements.

functions.name: regulation of target gene expression
functions.description: Regulation of target gene expression refers to the control of the level of gene product produced from a specific gene.

functions.name: Regulation of target genes
functions.description: The process by which miRNAs affect the expression of various target genes in the genome.

functions.name: Regulation of TE activity
functions.description: Mechanisms that control the expression and mobilization of transposable elements.

functions.name: regulation of totipotency
functions.description: Regulation of totipotency involves the control of a cell's ability to give rise to all cell types of an organism.

functions.name: Regulation of transcription
functions.description: The control of the rate at which genetic information is copied from DNA to RNA.

functions.name: Regulation of transcription initiation
functions.description: The process by which the start of gene transcription is controlled, which can be influenced by genomic repeat elements.

functions.name: Regulation of transposable element numbers
functions.description: Regulation of transposable element numbers is a proposed mechanism where nonautonomous elements control the copy numbers of autonomous elements.

functions.name: Regulatory element
functions.description: A regulatory element is a DNA sequence that controls the transcription of one or more genes.

functions.name: Regulatory element acquisition
functions.description: The process where LINE-1 loci with defunct promoters can acquire regulatory elements from nearby genes to restore retrotransposition activity.

functions.name: Regulatory evolution
functions.description: The evolutionary changes in the genomic regulatory landscape, including promoters and enhancers, across species or tissues.

functions.name: regulatory function
functions.description: Regulatory function refers to the role of elements in controlling gene expression.

functions.name: regulatory innovation
functions.description: The evolutionary creation of new gene regulatory functions or networks.

functions.name: Regulatory landscape remodeling
functions.description: The process by which the three-dimensional organization and regulatory interactions of a genomic region are altered.

functions.name: Regulatory network assembly
functions.description: Regulatory network assembly refers to the process of integrating various DNA sequences, including transposon-derived sequences, into cellular gene regulatory circuits.

functions.name: Regulatory protein encoding
functions.description: Regulatory protein encoding refers to the process where a transposon encodes a protein that can regulate biological processes.

functions.name: regulatory rewiring
functions.description: Regulatory rewiring involves changes in gene regulatory networks.

functions.name: Regulatory role
functions.description: A regulatory role refers to the function of a genomic element in controlling gene expression or other cellular processes.

functions.name: Regulatory roles
functions.description: Regulatory roles refer to the functions of transposable elements in controlling gene expression or other genomic processes.

functions.name: regulatory sequence turnover
functions.description: The evolutionary gain and loss of regulatory DNA sequences.

functions.name: Regulatory signature switching
functions.description: The evolutionary process where a genomic region changes its primary regulatory function, such as switching between promoter and enhancer activity.

functions.name: Reinfection
functions.description: Reinfection refers to the process by which exogenous retroviruses can integrate into the germline, contributing to the formation of HERVs.

functions.name: Relative expression
functions.description: Relative expression refers to the quantification of gene or element expression levels compared to a reference or control group.

functions.name: Repair of double-strand breaks
functions.description: Repair of double-strand breaks (DSBs) is a cellular process to fix DNA breaks, which can be mediated by reverse transcriptase.

functions.name: Repeat element dysregulation
functions.description: Repeat element dysregulation refers to the abnormal expression or suppression of repetitive sequences, including transposons, in pathological states.

functions.name: Repeat element expression
functions.description: Repeat element expression refers to the transcription of repetitive sequences, including transposons, in the genome.

functions.name: repeat element representation altered by epigenetic states
functions.description: The representation of repeat elements in the genome can be altered by changes in DNA methylation, histone modifications, or other epigenetic marks.

functions.name: repeat element representation altered by structural changes
functions.description: The representation of repeat elements in the genome can be altered by large-scale genomic rearrangements or structural variations.

functions.name: Repeat enrichment in gene promoters
functions.description: Repeat enrichment in gene promoters refers to the overrepresentation of repetitive elements in the regulatory regions of genes.

functions.name: Repeat expansion
functions.description: The pathological increase in the number of tandem repeat sequences, often associated with neurological diseases.

functions.name: Repeat expression
functions.description: Repeat expression refers to the transcriptional activity of repetitive DNA elements, including transposons.

functions.name: repeat length-dependent expansion
functions.description: Repeat length-dependent expansion describes the phenomenon where the propensity for a repeat tract to expand increases with its initial length.

functions.name: Repeat-induced gene activation (RIGA)
functions.description: Repeat-induced gene activation is a process where repeated sequences enhance gene expression.

functions.name: Repeat-induced gene silencing (RIGS)
functions.description: Repeat-induced gene silencing is a process where repeated sequences suppress gene expression.

functions.name: Repetitive element transcript expression
functions.description: The transcription of repetitive element sequences into RNA.

functions.name: replication
functions.description: Replication refers to the process by which transposable elements copy and insert themselves into new genomic locations.

functions.name: Replication mechanism
functions.description: The process by which retroposons copy and insert themselves into new genomic locations.

functions.name: Replication origin association
functions.description: Replication origin association refers to the localization of genomic elements within or near constitutive replication origins.

functions.name: Replication regulation
functions.description: Replication regulation refers to the control of the replication process of genetic elements, such as retroelements.

functions.name: replication stress
functions.description: Replication stress refers to the slowing or stalling of DNA replication forks, which can lead to genomic instability.

functions.name: replication-coupled DNA-repair
functions.description: Replication-coupled DNA-repair refers to DNA repair pathways that are coordinated with the DNA replication machinery.

functions.name: replication-fork restart
functions.description: Replication-fork restart is the process of resuming DNA synthesis after a stalled or collapsed replication fork.

functions.name: replication-stress signaling
functions.description: Replication-stress signaling involves cellular pathways that detect and respond to obstacles or damage during DNA replication.

functions.name: Replicative senescence
functions.description: A state of irreversible cell cycle arrest associated with aging and cellular stress.

functions.name: replicative transposition (mobilization)
functions.description: Replicative transposition is the process by which active L1 elements copy and paste themselves into new genomic locations, driving genetic diversity.

functions.name: repress transposable elements
functions.description: The process of inhibiting the activity or expression of transposable elements.

functions.name: Repression
functions.description: Repression is a form of gene or transposon expression regulation that decreases or silences transcription.

functions.name: Repression by DNA methylation
functions.description: The silencing of gene or transposon expression through the addition of methyl groups to cytosine bases in DNA.

functions.name: Repression by KRAB-ZNF proteins
functions.description: Repression by KRAB-ZNF proteins is a key defense mechanism in mammals that silences transposable elements to offer genomic protection.

functions.name: repression by KZNFs
functions.description: KRAB Zinc Finger Proteins (KZNFs) are a family of proteins that bind to and repress certain classes of repeat elements.

functions.name: Repression of L1 5' UTR
functions.description: HBV polymerase represses the activity of the L1 5' untranslated region.

functions.name: Repression of proximal genes
functions.description: The process of decreasing the transcription of genes located nearby.

functions.name: repression of retrotransposition
functions.description: Repression of retrotransposition refers to cellular mechanisms that suppress the activity of retrotransposons.

functions.name: Repression of retrotransposons
functions.description: Repression of retrotransposons is the silencing mechanism that controls their activity.

functions.name: Repression of transposable elements
functions.description: Repression of transposable elements refers to the epigenetic silencing of transposons to prevent their aberrant activity.

functions.name: repression of transposons
functions.description: Repression of transposons refers to the molecular mechanisms that inhibit the activity and mobility of transposable elements.

functions.name: Reprogramming
functions.description: Reprogramming refers to the process of converting somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) by expressing specific factors.

functions.name: Reprogramming of gene expression
functions.description: Reprogramming of gene expression refers to the alteration of gene expression patterns.

functions.name: Reprogramming transgene removal
functions.description: The process of excising transposon-delivered reprogramming transgenes from the genome of induced pluripotent stem cells.

functions.name: Reprogramming vector removal
functions.description: Reprogramming vector removal is a technique to eliminate exogenous genetic material used to induce pluripotency, ensuring the safety of the resulting iPSCs.

functions.name: Reshaping the genome
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposons alter the structure and composition of the genome.

functions.name: restraining totipotency
functions.description: Restraining totipotency refers to the process of limiting the developmental potential of naive human embryonic stem cells to a totipotent-like state.

functions.name: Restriction
functions.description: Restriction refers to the inhibition or limitation of the mobility or infectivity of retroelements and retroviruses.

functions.name: restriction of retrotransposons
functions.description: Restriction of retrotransposons refers to the cellular mechanisms that inhibit or control the mobilization of retrotransposable elements to maintain genomic stability.

functions.name: retention on the X chromosome
functions.description: The process of maintaining transposable elements, such as LINE-1, on the X chromosome, potentially through selection.

functions.name: reteoelement expression
functions.description: Retroelement expression refers to the transcription and potential activity of retrotransposons such as LINE-1 and HERVs.

functions.name: Retroduplication
functions.description: Retroduplication is the process involving reverse transcription of mRNAs and their insertion back into the genome.

functions.name: retroelement activation
functions.description: Retroelement activation is the process by which retrotransposons become transcriptionally active.

functions.name: retroelement amplification
functions.description: Retroelement amplification is the process by which retrotransposons increase their copy number in the genome.

functions.name: retroelement derepression
functions.description: Retroelement derepression is the loss of repression leading to increased expression of retrotransposons.

functions.name: retroelement integration
functions.description: Retroelement integration is the process by which retrotransposons insert into the genome.

functions.name: Retroelement silencing
functions.description: Retroelement silencing refers to the epigenetic and transcriptional mechanisms that repress the activity of retrotransposable elements in the genome.

functions.name: retroelement-induced mutagenesis
functions.description: Retroelement-induced mutagenesis refers to the molecular mechanisms by which retroelements cause human disease.

functions.name: Retrogene formation
functions.description: Retrogene formation is the creation of new genes through the retroposition of processed mRNA.

functions.name: retrohoming mechanism
functions.description: The mechanism by which mobile group II introns or related retrotransposons insert into a DNA target site via reverse splicing and reverse transcription.

functions.name: Retroposition
functions.description: Retroposition is the process by which retrotransposons insert new copies into the genome via an RNA intermediate.

functions.name: retroposon transposition
functions.description: Retroposon transposition is the process by which retroposons move and integrate into new genomic locations via reverse transcription of an RNA intermediate.

functions.name: retrotranscriptome
functions.description: The complete set of transcripts derived from retrotransposons, including HERVs, within a cell or tissue.

functions.name: Retrotransposable element (RTE) control
functions.description: Retrotransposable element control refers to the cellular mechanisms, such as siRNA silencing, that repress the activity of retrotransposons in somatic tissues.

functions.name: retrotransposal integration
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposable elements insert copies of themselves into new genomic locations via an RNA intermediate.

functions.name: retrotransposition
functions.description: Retrotransposition is the process by which LINE-1 elements move within the genome.

functions.name: retrotransposition at dysfunctional telomeres
functions.description: The process of LINE-1 retrotransposition events targeted to dysfunctional telomeres via the ENi pathway.

functions.name: Retrotransposition control
functions.description: Retrotransposition control refers to the host mechanisms that regulate or suppress the mobility of retrotransposable elements.

functions.name: Retrotransposition in cis
functions.description: Retrotransposition in cis is the process by which LINE-1 preferentially mobilizes its own encoding RNA.

functions.name: Retrotransposition in trans
functions.description: Retrotransposition in trans is the process by which LINE-1 proteins can mobilize non-self RNAs, such as Alu RNA or cellular mRNAs.

functions.name: Retrotransposition of endogenous genes
functions.description: Retrotransposition of endogenous genes refers to the process where cellular protein-coding genes are reverse-transcribed and reinserted into the genome, creating processed pseudogenes.

functions.name: Retrotransposition of processed pseudogenes
functions.description: The process by which cellular mRNAs are reverse transcribed and inserted into the nuclear genome by L1 machinery, creating processed pseudogenes.

functions.name: retrotransposition-dependent DNA mobilization
functions.description: Retrotransposition-dependent DNA mobilization is a mechanism by which retrotransposons move within the genome, leading to insertion mutations and DNA deletions.

functions.name: retrotransposition-independent consequences
functions.description: Effects of LINE-1 activity that do not require the element to move to a new location.

functions.name: retrotransposition-independent disruption of epithelial programming and differentiation
functions.description: Retrotransposition-independent disruption of epithelial programming and differentiation is a mechanism by which retrotransposons affect cellular processes without necessarily mobilizing.

functions.name: retrotransposition-mediated deletion
functions.description: Retrotransposition-mediated deletion is a mechanism of genome alteration created by retrotransposable elements.

functions.name: Retrotransposon abundance variation
functions.description: Retrotransposon abundance variation refers to differences in the copy number or genomic proportion of retrotransposons among individuals or populations.

functions.name: retrotransposon activation
functions.description: Retrotransposon activation refers to the process by which retrotransposons become transcriptionally and/or transpositionally active.

functions.name: Retrotransposon activity
functions.description: Retrotransposon activity refers to the transcription and mobilization of retrotransposons within the genome.

functions.name: Retrotransposon amplification
functions.description: Retrotransposon amplification refers to the process of increasing copy number through replication and insertion.

functions.name: Retrotransposon control
functions.description: Retrotransposon control refers to the cellular mechanisms that regulate the activity and mobility of retrotransposons.

functions.name: retrotransposon de-repression
functions.description: Retrotransposon de-repression refers to the loss of transcriptional silencing of retrotransposons, leading to their aberrant expression.

functions.name: Retrotransposon diversification
functions.description: The evolutionary process leading to the emergence of distinct retrotransposon lineages or families.

functions.name: Retrotransposon evolution
functions.description: Retrotransposon evolution refers to the process of change and diversification of retrotransposon families and subfamilies over time.

functions.name: retrotransposon expression
functions.description: The production of RNA transcripts from retrotransposon sequences.

functions.name: Retrotransposon expression upregulation
functions.description: An increase in the expression levels of retrotransposons.

functions.name: Retrotransposon extinction
functions.description: The loss of active retrotransposon lineages from a genome.

functions.name: retrotransposon hypomethylation
functions.description: Retrotransposon hypomethylation refers to a decrease in the methylation level of retrotransposon sequences, which can lead to their increased activity or expression.

functions.name: Retrotransposon insertion
functions.description: Retrotransposon insertion refers to the genomic integration event of a retrotransposon into a new location in the genome.

functions.name: Retrotransposon insertion polymorphism
functions.description: Retrotransposon insertion polymorphism refers to the presence or absence of non-reference transposable element variants in an individual's genome.

functions.name: Retrotransposon mobilization
functions.description: Retrotransposon mobilization is the process by which retrotransposons move to new genomic locations.

functions.name: Retrotransposon proliferation
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposons increase their copy number within the host genome, creating a tension with host survival.

functions.name: Retrotransposon propagation
functions.description: Retrotransposon propagation refers to the process by which retrotransposons, such as LINE-1, replicate and increase their copy number within the genome through a copy-and-paste mechanism.

functions.name: retrotransposon reactivation
functions.description: Retrotransposon reactivation refers to the process where normally silenced retrotransposons become transcriptionally active again.

functions.name: Retrotransposon recombination-mediated inversion (RRMI)
functions.description: Retrotransposon recombination-mediated inversion is a mechanism that causes chromosomal inversions without altering the amount of genomic material.

functions.name: retrotransposon regulation
functions.description: Retrotransposon regulation involves the control of retrotransposon activity and expression.

functions.name: retrotransposon repression
functions.description: Retrotransposon repression is the process of inhibiting the transcription or activity of retrotransposons.

functions.name: retrotransposon RNA expression
functions.description: Retrotransposon RNA expression refers to the transcription of retrotransposon elements into RNA.

functions.name: Retrotransposon RNA stability regulation
functions.description: Retrotransposon RNA stability regulation is the process by which the stability of retrotransposon RNA transcripts is controlled, affecting their potential for retrotransposition.

functions.name: Retrotransposon silencing
functions.description: Retrotransposon silencing refers to the cellular mechanisms that restrict the mobility and expression of retrotransposons.

functions.name: Retrotransposon transcription
functions.description: Retrotransposon transcription is the process of generating RNA transcripts from retrotransposon sequences.

functions.name: Retrotransposon transcription regulation
functions.description: Retrotransposon transcription regulation involves the control of the initiation and rate of transcription of retrotransposon elements from genomic DNA into RNA.

functions.name: Retrotransposon transcriptional silencing
functions.description: A host defense mechanism to repress retrotransposon transcription and prevent further insertions.

functions.name: Retrotransposon-mediated sequence transduction
functions.description: Retrotransposon-mediated sequence transduction is the process by which a retrotransposon carries flanking sequence during its mobilization, proposed as a gene duplication mechanism.

functions.name: retrotransposons activation
functions.description: Retrotransposons activation refers to the increased transcriptional and/or transpositional activity of retrotransposons.

functions.name: Retroviral deletion
functions.description: Retroviral deletion refers to the loss of endogenous retroviral sequences from the genome, which can occur over evolutionary time.

functions.name: Retroviral insertion
functions.description: Retroviral insertion is the process by which a retrovirus integrates its genetic material into the host genome.

functions.name: Retroviral insertion mutagenesis
functions.description: A process where the integration of a retroviral genome into the host DNA disrupts gene function or regulation, leading to mutations.

functions.name: Retroviral integration
functions.description: Retroviral integration is the process by which a retrovirus inserts its DNA copy into the host genome.

functions.name: Retroviral primer-binding site hybridization
functions.description: A method using synthetic oligonucleotides complementary to putative retroviral primer-binding sites as hybridization probes to detect novel retrovirus-like sequences.

functions.name: Retroviral provirus structure
functions.description: A genomic element with structural features characteristic of a retroviral provirus, including long terminal repeats and a pol gene.

functions.name: Retroviral transposition
functions.description: Retroviral transposition is a process by which retroviral-like elements move and insert into new genomic locations.

functions.name: reverse transcriptase (RT) enzyme expression
functions.description: The expression of the reverse transcriptase enzyme encoded by retrotransposons.

functions.name: Reverse transcriptase activity
functions.description: Reverse-transcriptase activity is the enzymatic function of converting RNA into DNA, which is utilized by retrotransposons.

functions.name: Reverse transcriptase expression
functions.description: Reverse transcriptase expression refers to the production of the enzyme that catalyzes the reverse transcription of RNA into DNA.

functions.name: reverse transcriptase inhibition
functions.description: The process of inhibiting the activity of reverse transcriptase (RT) enzymes.

functions.name: Reverse transcriptase-mediated DNA damage response
functions.description: Reverse transcriptase-mediated DNA damage response is a cellular response triggered by the reverse transcriptase activity of LINE-1 ORF2p, independent of its endonuclease activity.

functions.name: Reverse transcription
functions.description: The enzymatic process of synthesizing DNA from an RNA template, utilized by retrotransposons.

functions.name: Reverse transcription and integration
functions.description: Reverse transcription and integration is the process by which RNA is reverse transcribed into DNA and then inserted into a new genomic location.

functions.name: Reverse transcription by ORF2p
functions.description: ORF2p possesses reverse transcriptase activity and can use recruited cellular RNAs as templates.

functions.name: Reverse transcription of L1 RNA 5'-CAP
functions.description: A process that explains the higher frequency of G nucleotides observed upstream from the L1, likely involving the incorporation of the RNA cap during reverse transcription.

functions.name: reverse transcription priming
functions.description: Reverse transcription priming is the process where the nicked poly-T DNA strand generated by LINE-1 endonuclease serves as a primer for the reverse transcription of LINE-1 RNA.

functions.name: reverse transcriptional transposition
functions.description: Reverse transcriptional transposition is the process by which LINE-1 replicates and inserts itself into new gene sites through reverse transcription.

functions.name: reversible immortalization
functions.description: Reversible immortalization is a technique to enable continuous cell growth without senescence, which can later be reversed.

functions.name: Ribonuclease sensitivity
functions.description: The property of a complex being disrupted or dissociated upon treatment with ribonuclease.

functions.name: Ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex formation
functions.description: The process where L1-encoded proteins ORF1p and ORF2p bind to L1 RNA in cis to form a ribonucleoprotein complex essential for retrotransposition.

functions.name: Ribonucleoprotein (RNP) condensate formation
functions.description: Many copies of the ORF1p protein assemble onto the LINE-1 RNA to form a ribonucleoprotein (RNP) condensate.

functions.name: Ribonucleoprotein (RNP) formation
functions.description: Ribonucleoprotein (RNP) formation is the process where the full-length LINE-1 transcript assembles in cis with its encoded proteins ORF1p and ORF2p.

functions.name: ribonucleoprotein particle (RNP) disruption
functions.description: Ribonucleoprotein particle (RNP) disruption refers to the impairment of the functional complex formed by LINE-1 RNA and proteins (ORF1p, ORF2p), which is essential for retrotransposition.

functions.name: ribonucleoprotein particle assembly
functions.description: Ribonucleoprotein particle assembly is the formation of a complex containing L1 RNA, ORF1p, and ORF2p, which is the core of the LINE-1 retrotransposition machinery.

functions.name: ribonucleoprotein particle formation
functions.description: Ribonucleoprotein particle formation is the assembly of RNA and proteins, which is a step in the retrotransposition cycle of LINE-1.

functions.name: Ribonucleoprotein particle transport
functions.description: Ribonucleoprotein particle transport is the movement of ribonucleoprotein complexes within the cell.

functions.name: Ribonucleotide Excision Repair (RER)
functions.description: Ribonucleotide Excision Repair (RER) is a pathway that completes the removal of ribonucleoside monophosphates (rNMPs) from DNA after incision by RNase H2.

functions.name: Ribosomal association
functions.description: Ribosomal association is the process by which Alu RNA interacts with ribosomes.

functions.name: Ribosome stalling
functions.description: Ribosome stalling is a condition where the ribosome pauses during translation elongation, which is recognized by the Alu ribonucleoprotein particle.

functions.name: RIG-I-like receptor (RLR)-associated type-I interferon signaling
functions.description: RIG-I-like receptor (RLR)-associated type-I interferon signaling is an innate immune pathway triggered by detection of viral or endogenous dsRNA.

functions.name: RNA 3'-end polyadenylation
functions.description: RNA 3'-end polyadenylation is the addition of a poly(A) tail to the 3' end of an RNA molecule.

functions.name: RNA 3'-end uridylation
functions.description: RNA 3'-end uridylation is the addition of uridine residues to the 3' end of an RNA molecule.

functions.name: RNA binding
functions.description: LINE-1 ORF1 protein (ORF1p) is an RNA-binding protein that binds to L1 RNA.

functions.name: RNA chaperone activity
functions.description: LINE-1 ORF1 protein (ORF1p) acts as an RNA chaperone, which is required for retrotransposition.

functions.name: RNA circularization
functions.description: RNA circularization is a process where the ends of an RNA molecule are joined to form a circle.

functions.name: RNA circularization via Alu/Alu base-pairing
functions.description: A process where Alu sequences located in flanking introns base-pair with each other, facilitating the formation of circular RNA molecules from exons.

functions.name: RNA decay
functions.description: RNA decay is the process of RNA degradation.

functions.name: RNA degradation
functions.description: RNA degradation is a cellular pathway that breaks down RNA molecules, serving as a regulatory mechanism to control the expression of retrotransposons.

functions.name: RNA duplex formation
functions.description: RNA duplex formation is the process where complementary RNA strands base-pair to form a double-stranded structure.

functions.name: RNA expression
functions.description: The process of transcribing DNA sequences into RNA molecules.

functions.name: RNA interference (RNAi)
functions.description: RNA interference is a mechanism of gene silencing triggered by small interfering RNAs.

functions.name: RNA interference (RNAi) by antisense ORF0 RNA
functions.description: RNA interference by antisense ORF0 RNA is a potential regulatory mechanism targeting LINE-1 RNA.

functions.name: RNA ligation
functions.description: A known mechanism potentially involved in the formation of LINE-1 chimeric insertions.

functions.name: RNA m6A modification
functions.description: A common post-transcriptional RNA modification, involving methylation at the N6 position of adenosine.

functions.name: RNA metabolism
functions.description: A recurring theme for retrotransposons is their tie-in to RNA metabolism, as they mobilize via RNA intermediates.

functions.name: RNA methylation
functions.description: RNA methylation is a chemical modification of RNA molecules, such as N6-methyladenosine (m6A).

functions.name: RNA packaging
functions.description: RNA packaging is a function performed by the L1ORF1 protein during LINE-1 retrotransposition.

functions.name: RNA polymerase II activity
functions.description: The transcriptional activity of RNA polymerase II, the enzyme responsible for synthesizing mRNA and other non-coding RNAs.

functions.name: RNA polymerase II enrichment
functions.description: The accumulation of RNA polymerase II at specific genomic loci.

functions.name: RNA polymerase II transcription
functions.description: A transcription process regulated by motifs such as CCAAT, TATA, and ATTAAA found in long terminal repeats.

functions.name: RNA polymerase II-driven transcription
functions.description: Transcription of LINE-1 elements is driven by an internal RNA polymerase II promoter.

functions.name: RNA polymerase III transcription
functions.description: RNA polymerase III transcription is the process by which RNA polymerase III synthesizes small, non-coding RNAs, including some from transposable elements.

functions.name: RNA polymerase III-dependent transcription
functions.description: A transcription process mediated by RNA polymerase III, which is sensitive to the inhibitor tagetitoxin.

functions.name: RNA polymerase III-driven transcription
functions.description: Transcription of SINE elements like Alu is driven by an internal RNA polymerase III promoter.

functions.name: RNA processing
functions.description: RNA processing encompasses the modifications an RNA molecule undergoes after transcription, such as splicing, editing, and polyadenylation.

functions.name: RNA quality control
functions.description: RNA quality control refers to cellular mechanisms that ensure the fidelity and proper processing of RNA molecules.

functions.name: RNA recognition by LINE-1 reverse transcriptase
functions.description: The mechanism by which the LINE-1-encoded reverse transcriptase (RT) specifically recognizes its own RNA and Alu RNA for retrotransposition.

functions.name: RNA recombination
functions.description: RNA recombination is a process involving the exchange of genetic material between RNA molecules.

functions.name: RNA recruitment to L1-RNP
functions.description: The RNA-binding property of ORF1p is critical to recruit other mobile RNAs to the L1-ribonucleoprotein particle.

functions.name: RNA secondary structure disruption
functions.description: RNA secondary structure disruption refers to the alteration of the base-pairing patterns within an RNA molecule, which can affect its function and interactions.

functions.name: RNA sensing pathways
functions.description: RNA sensing pathways are innate immune signaling cascades that detect foreign or aberrant RNA, such as those mediated by RIG-I and MDA5.

functions.name: RNA splicing
functions.description: RNA splicing is the process of removing introns from a pre-mRNA transcript and joining exons together.

functions.name: RNA stability
functions.description: The resistance of an RNA molecule to degradation, influencing its availability for processes like retrotransposition.

functions.name: RNA stability regulation
functions.description: RNA stability regulation refers to the processes that control the degradation or stabilization of RNA molecules, influencing their half-life and abundance.

functions.name: RNA surveillance
functions.description: RNA surveillance refers to cellular mechanisms that monitor and degrade aberrant or nonsense RNAs.

functions.name: RNA targeting
functions.description: RNA targeting refers to the process of directing or localizing RNA molecules to specific cellular locations or complexes.

functions.name: RNA template switching
functions.description: A process during reverse transcription where the reverse transcriptase switches from one RNA template to another, leading to the formation of chimeric cDNA.

functions.name: RNA transcript production
functions.description: RNA transcript production is the generation of RNA molecules from a DNA sequence, which is a key step in gene expression.

functions.name: RNA truncation
functions.description: RNA truncation refers to the generation of shortened RNA transcripts, often due to premature termination of transcription.

functions.name: RNA-chromatin crosstalk
functions.description: RNA-chromatin crosstalk describes the interaction and mutual regulation between RNA molecules and chromatin structure during cell fate transitions.

functions.name: RNA-DNA hybrid formation
functions.description: RNA-DNA hybrid formation is the generation of structures where an RNA strand is base-paired with a complementary DNA strand.

functions.name: RNA-guided transposition
functions.description: RNA-guided transposition is a process where transposase activity is directed to specific genomic sequences using guide RNAs.

functions.name: RNA-mediated DNA repair
functions.description: A proposed ancestral mechanism associated with non-LTR retrotransposons that may have been used before the acquisition of an endonuclease domain.

functions.name: RNA-mediated gene insertion
functions.description: RNA-mediated gene insertion is a process where genetic material is delivered and integrated into the genome via an RNA intermediate.

functions.name: RNA-mediated genomic invasion
functions.description: The process by which retrotransposon RNAs and cellular mRNAs are reverse transcribed and integrated into genomic DNA.

functions.name: RNA-protein complex formation
functions.description: The process where SINE-derived RNAs interact with cellular proteins to form ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes.

functions.name: RNA-RNA interaction
functions.description: RNA-RNA interaction refers to the direct physical association between different RNA molecules.

functions.name: RNA-RNA recombination
functions.description: RNA-RNA recombination is a process that occurs during L1 reverse transcription, leading to the formation of chimeric retrotranscripts.

functions.name: RNA-sensing response
functions.description: An innate immune response triggered by sensing of RNA, mediated through MAVS signaling.

functions.name: RNA-seq analysis
functions.description: A method using next-generation sequencing to measure RNA expression levels.

functions.name: RNA/DNA hybrid processing
functions.description: RNA/DNA hybrid processing refers to the cleavage of the RNA strand in RNA/DNA hybrids, a function shared by RNase H1 and RNase H2.

functions.name: RNA:DNA heteroduplex formation
functions.description: RNA:DNA heteroduplex formation is the process where an RNA strand base-pairs with a complementary DNA strand.

functions.name: RNA:DNA hybrid formation
functions.description: RNA:DNA hybrid formation is the generation of duplex structures composed of one RNA strand and one DNA strand.

functions.name: RNase H activity
functions.description: A putative function associated with the 3'-end domain of the LINE ORF2 protein, dispensable for reverse transcription in this assay.

functions.name: RNP complex assembly
functions.description: RNP complex assembly refers to the formation of ribonucleoprotein particles containing L1 RNA and the encoded proteins ORF1p and ORF2p.

functions.name: RNP complex formation
functions.description: ORF1p packages its transcript into an ORF2p-containing ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex, which is the retrotransposition intermediate.

functions.name: RNP formation
functions.description: RNP (ribonucleoprotein) formation is the assembly of LINE-1 RNA with its encoded proteins, which is a critical step in the retrotransposition cycle.

functions.name: RNP sequestration in cytoplasmic bodies
functions.description: RNP sequestration in cytoplasmic bodies involves the compartmentalization of ribonucleoprotein complexes, potentially to limit their activity.

functions.name: RT-dependent mechanism in tumorigenesis
functions.description: A mechanism that operates in tumorigenesis and is dependent on reverse transcriptase activity.

functions.name: RT-dependent regulatory mechanism
functions.description: A regulatory mechanism that operates during preimplantation development, is repressed in normal tissues, and when reactivated, promotes cell transformation and cancer progression.

functions.name: RT-mediated somatic gene recombination/retroinsertion
functions.description: RT-mediated somatic gene recombination/retroinsertion is a process where reverse transcriptase activity facilitates the insertion or recombination of genetic material in somatic cells.

functions.name: RTE de-repression
functions.description: RTE de-repression is the loss of normal silencing mechanisms, leading to increased activity of retrotransposable elements.

functions.name: S phase
functions.description: S phase is the stage of the cell cycle when DNA replication occurs and when LINE-1 retrotransposition peaks.

functions.name: S-phase insertion
functions.description: A proposed mechanism for the nonrandom genomic distribution of transposons based on insertion timing during DNA replication.

functions.name: S/G2 phase DNA repair
functions.description: S/G2 phase DNA repair refers to DNA repair mechanisms that are active during the S and G2 phases of the cell cycle.

functions.name: Seamless genome editing
functions.description: Seamless genome editing is a technique for introducing precise genetic modifications, such as point mutations, without leaving exogenous DNA sequences like selection markers at the target locus.

functions.name: seamless removal of selection markers
functions.description: The process of excising genetic selection markers from the genome without leaving behind unwanted sequences.

functions.name: Second-strand cleavage
functions.description: Second-strand cleavage is the rate-limiting catalytic step in the transposition reaction of Hsmar1.

functions.name: second-strand DNA synthesis
functions.description: The synthesis of the complementary DNA strand following reverse transcription to generate a double-stranded DNA copy.

functions.name: Segmental duplication
functions.description: Segmental duplication is a genomic event involving the copying and insertion of a large DNA segment, often containing genes and repeats.

functions.name: Segmental duplication (SD) mobilization
functions.description: Segmental duplication mobilization is the process by which large, duplicated genomic segments are propagated and rearranged.

functions.name: Segmental genomic duplication
functions.description: A process involving the duplication of large genomic regions, which can confound the identification of unique L1 insertion events.

functions.name: Selection

functions.name: selection system

functions.name: selective repression

functions.name: self-propagation

functions.name: Self-renewal

functions.name: Self-renewal maintenance

functions.name: self-replication

functions.name: senescence

functions.name: Senescence-associated chromatin rewiring

functions.name: senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)

functions.name: senescence-like phenotype

functions.name: sense transcription

functions.name: Sequence amplification

functions.name: Sequence diversification

functions.name: sequence diversity accumulation

functions.name: Sequence homology

functions.name: Sequence transduction

functions.name: Sequence-specific DNA binding

functions.name: Sequence-specific insertion
